title: High school protests across France with marches in Lille, Marseille and Paris blockades
content:
Student protests continue across France, with marches taking place in cities including Lille and Marseille. In Paris, pupils staged fresh school blockades, using wheelie bins to obstruct school entrances.

The demonstrators are calling for better learning conditions. They say that government measures announced so far have failed to address their concerns.
summary: Student protests continued across France with marches in cities such as Lille and Marseille and fresh school blockades in Paris using wheelie bins. Demonstrators said they are demanding better learning conditions and claim government measures announced so far have not addressed their concerns.
author: France 24

title: France sees 480,000 students protest nationwide, Paris demo ends with tear gas and fires
content:
Around 480,000 people participated in nationwide student demonstrations across France on Tuesday, according to student and school unions, marking an increase from the previous week’s mobilisation.

In Paris, the protest escalated and concluded with the deployment of tear gas and the outbreak of fires as tensions rose.

Claire Paccalin reported the latest developments.
summary: Around 480,000 people took part in nationwide student demonstrations across France on Tuesday, according to student and school unions. In Paris, the demonstration ended with tear gas and fires as tensions escalated.
author: France 24

title: Germany seeks stronger EU trade‑defence as China import pressure outweighs export gains
content:
Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, citing concerns that such moves could provoke retaliation.  

Recent pressure on key German industries, however, has altered the country’s approach. The rise in import pressures has begun to eclipse the benefits Germany has gained from Chinese exports.  

In response, Berlin is now seeking stronger trade‑defense powers from the European Union to safeguard its industrial base.
summary: Germany has long resisted tougher action against China, fearing retaliation. Rising pressure on key industries has pushed Berlin to seek stronger EU trade‑defence powers to protect its industrial base.
author: DW World

title: Slovakia restores military-diplomatic ties with Russia for first time since 2022
content:
Slovakia has announced the restoration of military‑diplomatic relations with Russia, the first such engagement since 2022.  

The Slovak government has defended the decision, stating it is a step toward normalizing ties with the Russian Federation.  

Critics, however, warn that the move could expose Slovakia to espionage risks and may further erode trust within NATO.
summary: Slovakia is restoring military-diplomatic relations with Russia for the first time since 2022. Critics say the move raises espionage risks and could further erode trust within NATO, while the government defends the decision.
author: DW World

title: Youth-led protests against India's election chief trigger mass arrests and capital lockdown
content:
India: Can 'cockroaches' threaten Modi's political grip?

Thousands of protesters were detained, leaders were arrested upon arrival, and a capital city was placed under lockdown as the youth‑led protests against the election chief drew the attention of the Indian government.  

Experts say that while the protests have disrupted the capital, toppling the political structure remains a different challenge.
summary: Thousands were detained, leaders were arrested on arrival, and the capital was placed under lockdown as youth-led protests against the election chief attracted government attention. Experts say that toppling the election chief remains unlikely.

title: Kabila Joins Rwandan-Backed M23 Front, Raising Peace Concerns
content:
Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political‑military front that unites the Rwandan‑backed AFC/M23 coalition. The move brings Kabila into a broader alliance that could alter the dynamics of opposition politics in the country.

Analysts note that the coalition’s inclusion of a former president may strengthen its influence and provide a more organized platform for dissent against the current administration. The front’s alignment with the AFC/M23, already backed by Rwanda, positions it as a significant player in the national political landscape.

The development is seen as a potential reshaping of opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi, according to expert commentary.
summary: Former DR Congo President Joseph Kabila has joined a new political-military front that brings together the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 coalition. Analysts say the move could reshape opposition to President Felix Tshisekedi.
author: DW World

title: Scandal in Brazil’s top court could aid Flávio Bolsonaro and the Bolsonaro family
content:
A scandal surrounding Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, the judge who helped convict former president Jair Bolsonaro, is being framed as a political opportunity for Bolsonaro’s son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.  

At a rally of thousands of far‑right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, Brazil’s Independence Day, Flávio Bolsonaro warned voters that “whoever votes for Lula is voting for Alexandre de Moraes,” shifting focus from President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva to the embattled justice.  

Marina Silva has criticized Flávio Bolsonaro, saying he will try to finish his father’s “perverse project” to destroy the Amazon, underscoring the political tension linked to the court’s crisis.
summary: A crisis involving the judge who helped convict Jair Bolsonaro may benefit his son Flávio Bolsonaro and harm President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Flávio Bolsonaro addressed thousands of far‑right supporters in São Paulo on 7 September, warning that voting for Lula is a vote for Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

title: UK asks Interpol to reject Argentina's politically motivated Falklands oil arrest requests
content:
Britain has formally asked Interpol to reject Argentina’s “red notice” requests to arrest individuals linked to a large oil project off the Falkland Islands. The appeals cite the requests as politically motivated and stem from the administration of Argentine President Javier Milei.

UK officials say the requests come amid heightened tensions over the sovereignty of the British overseas territory, with the dispute reaching levels not seen since the 1982 war between the two countries. They have sought urgent assurances from Interpol that the notices will not be acted upon.
summary: Britain has appealed to Interpol to reject Argentina's red‑notice requests to arrest individuals linked to a large oil project off the Falkland Islands. UK officials say the requests are politically motivated and have asked Interpol for urgent assurances amid heightened sovereignty tensions.
author: Guardian World

Explosions were reported in Sanaa shortly after the Saudi‑led coalition issued an evacuation order for the city. In response, the Houthis pledged a “harsh” reaction to the coalition’s actions.

title: Men’s Rugby League World Cup 2026: group-by-group preview
content:
The Men’s Rugby League World Cup 2026 begins this week with a new format featuring ten teams and only four semi-final spots. Australia and New Zealand are positioned as the main contenders on home soil, while England faces increased pressure under the new structure. The competition has removed the quarter-final stage, replacing it with a complex group system.

In this new format, the four teams in Group A will compete for two of the semi-final places. The remaining six nations are split into three-team Groups B and C, where teams from Group B play against those in Group C and vice versa. The top two teams from the combined table of these two pools will advance to the semi-finals.
summary: Australia and New Zealand are main contenders on home soil while pressure is straight on England in new formatThe Rugby League World Cup returns with a new format and a new feel this week, but in the men’s event there is a familiar clutch of nations vying for glory. Ten teams will compete in a complex group format, with only four semi-final spots on offer after the quarter-final stage was removed.

title: Athletics powerless to act after Ruth Chepngetich's failed doping test
content:
Ruth Chepngetich’s failed doping test, which occurred five months after she set the women’s marathon world record in 2024, has left the sport uneasy but unable to take immediate action. The Kenyan runner recorded a time of 2 hours, 9 minutes, and 56 seconds in Chicago, a performance that broke the previous world record by 1 minute and 57 seconds and improved her personal best by five minutes.

NBC commentators compared the historic run to the moon landing, with one exclaiming, “Bring it on Neil Armstrong!” while another noted, “She has done things in this sport that we have not seen.” Following the race, Chepngetich responded to Robert Johnson of Let’s Run about accusations of doping by stating, “People must talk. I don’t know.”
summary: Ruth Chepngetich failed a doping test five months after setting the women's marathon world record. The article notes that this result left the sport deeply uneasy but unable to take action.

content:

On Friday, Newsom publicly supported Proposition 42, which seeks to prohibit retroactive taxes imposed by Proposition 40, the Billionaire Tax Act.

title: Massachusetts voters decide if cities must allow smaller homes on smaller lots
content:
Massachusetts voters will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. The measure would mandate that municipalities permit the construction of more compact housing units.

The proposal follows a growing trend in other states that are adopting similar rules to help ease a housing shortage.
summary: Voters in Massachusetts will decide whether to require cities and towns to allow smaller homes on smaller lots. A growing number of states are doing the same to help ease a housing shortage.

content:
With Election Day just a few weeks away and millions of votes already cast, midterm polls have become ubiquitous. The surge in polling reflects heightened public interest as the election approaches.

Analysts note that while polling can serve as a useful tool for gauging the electorate, it is not a definitive predictor of outcomes.
summary: Midterm polls are appearing widely as Election Day approaches with millions of votes already cast. The article notes that polling can help understand the electorate but is not a crystal ball.

content:

title: Prime Minister Ready to Debate Brexit Unflinchingly, Says BBC Political Editor
content:

Mason said the Prime Minister would “unflinchingly” debate the issue, marking a departure from the silence that has characterized previous administrations.  

The statement underscores a renewed willingness to address Brexit matters at the highest level of government.
summary: BBC political editor Chris Mason says the prime minister will unflinchingly debate Brexit. This is the first time a prime minister has taken such a stance since the UK left the EU.

title: Coastal erosion in England claims 183 homes over 16 years
content:
Coastal erosion in England has claimed at least 183 homes over the past 16 years, according to figures obtained by the Guardian. The losses have occurred along the east coast of the country, where homes have been lost to erosion and landslides.

The affected areas include communities in Yorkshire and East Anglia. Local councils have assessed properties along these coasts and determined that some were too vulnerable to remain safely occupied.

In response, councils have proactively demolished the identified homes to mitigate future risk.
summary: Seaside communities along England's east coast have lost at least 183 homes to coastal erosion and landslides over the past 16 years, according to figures obtained by the Guardian. Councils judged the properties on the Yorkshire and East Anglian coasts too vulnerable and proactively demolished them.

title: Tough Materials Reveal Variations in Histotripsy Outcomes Despite Same Duty Cycle
content:
Same duty cycle, very different outcomes: What tough materials taught us about histotripsy

During a Ph.D., the author wondered why some tissues are harder to break down with histotripsy than others.  

Histotripsy is a focused ultrasound technique that uses cavitation bubbles to mechanically break down tissue. Unlike thermal ablation, the goal is not to heat the tissue.  

Instead, the rapid activity of these bubbles creates mechanical stresses that progressively disrupt tissue structure.
summary: The author questioned why certain tissues are harder to break down with histotripsy. Histotripsy uses focused ultrasound and cavitation bubbles to mechanically disrupt tissue through rapid bubble activity, creating mechanical stresses instead of heating.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Extreme heat increases pregnancy complications, survey shows
content:
Extreme heat has led to a marked increase in the risks faced by pregnant women and their babies, a survey of 1,000 health care professionals has revealed. The study surveyed doctors and other medical staff in several countries, including Brazil, India and Zimbabwe, and found that rising temperatures are associated with higher complication rates during pregnancy.

The survey’s respondents reported that extreme heat conditions exacerbate health problems for expectant mothers, potentially affecting both maternal and infant outcomes. The findings highlight the growing impact of climate change on prenatal health in diverse global settings.
summary: Extreme heat has increased the risks for pregnant women and their babies. A survey of 1,000 health care professionals in Brazil, India and Zimbabwe found this effect.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Research Finds 17% of Physicians Report Disabilities, Calls for Accessible Workforce
content:
Physicians have disabilities too, a new study published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal reports. The research found that 5% of practicing physicians say they experience a disability “always or often,” while an additional 12% report a disability “sometimes.”

The authors argue that these findings highlight a need for greater accessibility within the medical workforce. They call for action to improve accommodations and support systems, aiming to promote equity and sustainability among physicians.
summary: The study, published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal, reports that 5% of practicing physicians always or often have a disability and an additional 12% sometimes have a disability. The authors call for action to improve accessibility and promote equity and sustainability in the physician workforce.

content:

An analysis published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal (CMAJ) argues that the act should be passed and highlights several factors the country should consider in its implementation.
summary: An analysis article in the Canadian Medical Association Journal argues that Canada’s proposed Safe Social Media Act should be passed. The article notes that the act aims to protect children and identifies several factors the country should consider.

title: Pancreatic cancer cells evolve to evade treatment and spread
content: Scientists analyzed nearly half a million cells from dozens of patients’ tumors and found that cancer cells continuously reshape their genetic makeup over time. The study shows that this ongoing evolution enables the cells to evade treatment for one of the deadliest forms of cancer. The findings highlight the challenge of treating pancreatic cancer, a disease known for its high mortality.
summary: An analysis of nearly half a million cells from dozens of patients' tumors shows that pancreatic cancer cells continuously reshape their genetic makeup over time. This evolution enables them to evade treatment.
author: Medical Xpress

content:

The IMF’s outlook suggests stronger growth in the near term, but the anticipated increase in energy costs and rates in 2027 could pose challenges for the upcoming fiscal plan.

title: Women ‘more likely to be told autoimmune conditions are psychological’
content:
A study by Cambridge University found a pronounced gender gap in how autoimmune conditions are diagnosed. Women with these illnesses are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic and experience considerably longer waits for both diagnosis and treatment.

The research highlights that autoimmune disorders affect hundreds of millions of people worldwide—about one in ten globally—and can produce symptoms such as fatigue, muscle pain and rashes. The findings suggest that misdiagnosis and delayed care disproportionately impact women.
summary: Cambridge University study suggests stark gender divide in misdiagnosis, with women also waiting longer for treatmentWomen with autoimmune conditions are up to 74% more likely than men to be told their symptoms are psychological or psychosomatic, and face much longer waits for a diagnosis and treatment, a study suggests. title: French supermarket director apologises after cyber‑attack spoils fresh and frozen food
content:
A cyber‑attack on Monday night caused refrigeration units in several hundred French supermarkets to heat up to 50 °C, leading to widespread loss of fresh and frozen food.  

At Intermarché La Haye, the breach raised fridge temperatures to 27 °C (80 °F), spoiling all perishable items. Store director Julien Freret said, “Today, we have a total loss of fresh and frozen,” and apologized to customers, calling the incident “an enormous loss of products.”  

The temperature spikes affected multiple locations across France, prompting the unprecedented heating of supermarket fridges and extensive product waste.
summary: A cyber‑attack raised refrigeration temperatures to as high as 50 °C overnight on Monday in hundreds of French supermarkets, causing widespread food loss. At Intermarché La Haye, temperatures reached 27 °C, spoiling fresh and frozen items, and store director Julien Freret apologized and called it an enormous loss of products.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Yerevan rents jump 23.5% to €800‑900 as Russians flee; Tbilisi rents level off
content:
Rents are climbing in Georgia and Armenia as Russian residents leave the region fearing mobilisation.  

In Yerevan, monthly rent for a two‑room flat has risen to €800–900, a 23.5 % increase year on year as of August.  

In Tbilisi, rents have levelled after earlier surges of 60–70 % that followed the full‑scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.  

Russian nationals now make up 72 % of all foreign property transactions in Armenia.
summary: Monthly rents for a two‑room flat in Yerevan have risen to €800‑900, a 23.5% year‑on‑year increase in August. Tbilisi rents have stabilised after earlier 60‑70% jumps, and Russian nationals make up 72% of foreign property transactions in Armenia.
author: Euronews

title: Morning news bulletin covers top European and global stories on Oct 13, 2026
content:
A news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin | October 13th, 2026 – Morning” was released on the morning of October 13, 2026. The bulletin invites readers to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond on that date.

It highlights coverage across a range of sections, including breaking news, world affairs, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
summary: The bulletin provides a roundup of the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 13, 2026. It includes coverage of world, business, entertainment, politics, culture, and travel news.
author: Euronews

title: US theme park operator Six Flags shuts nine roller coasters after man dies
content:
Six Flags, a U.S. theme‑park operator, shut down nine of its roller coasters after a man died.  

Police are investigating the incident, and television footage captured riders being evacuated from the 60‑metre‑high Goliath ride.  

The operator’s decision to close the nine coasters follows the fatality and the ongoing police inquiry.
summary: Six Flags shut nine roller coasters after a man died. Police are investigating after TV footage showed riders being evacuated from the 60‑metre high Goliath ride.
author: Euronews

title: Actress Selma Blair accused of punching and biting flight attendants on NY flight
content:
US actress Selma Blair, 54, has been accused of attacking cabin crew members on a flight to New York.  

According to U.S. media reports, Blair punched one flight attendant and bit another during the trip. After the flight, she reportedly assaulted a police officer and a nurse while being transported to a hospital. The incidents occurred on the flight and during the subsequent medical transport.
summary: US media reported that Blair, 54, punched one flight attendant and bit another during a flight to New York. She then allegedly assaulted a police officer and a nurse while being taken to the hospital.
author: Euronews

title: German nationals airlifted as storms kill five in Mexico's Baja California and Guerrero
content:
German nationals were among the people airlifted to safety as storms in Mexico killed five individuals. Heavy rain and strong winds caused serious damage in the states of Baja California and Guerrero.

Authorities in the affected regions are searching for six missing persons and have deployed thousands of rescue workers to address the damage and mitigate further flood risk. The ongoing response focuses on evacuations, rescue operations and monitoring of additional flooding threats.
summary: Heavy rain and strong winds caused serious damage in Baja California and Guerrero, killing five and airlifting German nationals to safety. Authorities seek six missing and have deployed thousands of rescue workers amid further flood risk.
author: Euronews

title: Ceuta prepares for King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia's visit after summer migration crisis
content:
Ceuta is preparing for a symbolic visit by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia following a mass migration crisis that has strained the enclave’s social cohesion.  

Officials say the royal trip comes as the city seeks to address the challenges posed by the recent influx of migrants and to reinforce community stability.
summary: Ceuta is bracing for a symbolic royal visit by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia. The visit follows a mass migration crisis that strained the enclave’s social cohesion.
author: Euronews

title: Rehman Baba Express derailment near Multan kills at least five, injures over 30
content:
A passenger train derailed near Multan, Pakistan, early on Tuesday, 13 October, killing at least five people and injuring more than 30. The incident involved the Rehman Baba Express.

Authorities have opened an investigation to determine the cause of the derailment.
summary: At least five people were killed and more than 30 injured when the Rehman Baba Express derailed near Multan, Pakistan, early on Tuesday, 13 October. An investigation has been launched into the cause of the accident.
author: Euronews

title: Russia claims EU purchased $320.7 billion of Russian energy since 2022
content:
Russia announced on Monday that European Union member states have purchased $320.7 billion in Russian energy resources since 2022, despite sanctions imposed because of the war in Ukraine.  

The disclosed amount has heightened tensions, with European officials criticizing a United States arrangement to import Russian diesel. At the same time, Sweden urged the bloc to employ frozen Russian assets to increase assistance for Kyiv.  

The statements underscore ongoing disputes over Russia’s energy trade with Europe amid the broader geopolitical conflict.
summary: Russia said on Monday that European Union countries had bought $320.7 billion worth of its energy resources since 2022, despite sanctions over the war in Ukraine. The claim came as European officials criticised a US deal to import Russian diesel and Sweden urged the bloc to use frozen Russian assets to boost support for Kyiv.
author: France 24

title: IMF upgrades 2026 growth forecast, notes split outlook for low‑income nations
content:
The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday that its forecast for global growth in 2026 has been upgraded, indicating the slowdown will be less pronounced than previously expected.  

The IMF attributed the revision to the “resilience” of advanced economies despite war‑fuelled energy prices, while cautioning that low‑income countries remain vulnerable to the ongoing supply shock.
summary: The International Monetary Fund on Tuesday forecast global growth in 2026 would slow less than previously expected because of advanced economies' resilience to war‑fuelled energy prices. It warned that low‑income countries remained vulnerable to the supply shock.
author: France 24

title: Greta Thunberg joins French student protests outside Paris high school
content:
Greta Thunberg joined French student protesters ahead of nationwide rallies scheduled for Tuesday.  

France is facing fresh demonstrations as students, unions and opposition groups rally over poor school conditions, including teacher shortages and dilapidated buildings.  

The Swedish activist stood with protesters outside a blockaded high school near Paris, raising the movement’s visibility. Authorities warn that violence is intensifying, even as the number of school closures has declined.  

Follow the liveblog for the latest updates.
summary: France is preparing fresh nationwide demonstrations on Tuesday as students, unions and opposition groups rally over poor school conditions such as teacher shortages and dilapidated buildings. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg joined protesters outside a blockaded high school near Paris, and authorities warned that violence is intensifying despite a decline in school closures.
author: France 24

title: France prepares for nationwide student protests over classroom conditions
content:
France prepared for nationwide demonstrations on Tuesday as students continued to protest poor classroom conditions.  

The mobilisation, backed by trade unions and the far‑left France Unbowed party, includes a march in Paris and rallies in other cities.  

Blockades had already disrupted central Paris, and authorities and protesters remain concerned about possible violence.
summary: France prepared for nationwide demonstrations on Tuesday as students continued protesting poor classroom conditions. Supported by trade unions and the far‑left France Unbowed party, the mobilisation includes a march in Paris and rallies in other cities, with blockades already disrupting central Paris and concerns about possible violence.
author: France 24

title: Argentina Temporarily Closes Iguazu Falls Amid El Niño‑Driven Water Surge
content:
Argentina’s Iguazu Falls were temporarily closed to tourists on Monday after an El Niño‑driven surge in water levels raised safety concerns. Heavy rain caused the Iguazu River to flow at more than six times its normal rate, prompting officials to act to prevent the river from bursting its banks.

National park authorities limited access when the river’s flow surpassed 12,000 cubic metres per second, a level far above the average. The precautionary closure was intended to protect visitors amid the rapid rise in water.
summary: National park officials closed tourist access to Iguazu Falls on Monday after the Iguazu River’s flow exceeded 12,000 cubic metres per second, more than six times its average rate. The closure was triggered by heavy rainfall from a supersized El Niño weather pattern that raised water levels and raised fears the river could burst its banks.
author: Guardian World

title: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel kill five on Mexico's Pacific coast
content:
Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel have killed at least five people as they battered Mexico’s Pacific coast. The storms triggered flash flooding that downed trees and electricity poles, blocked roads and inundated homes across the region.

Security forces deployed helicopters to rescue dozens of residents from the affected areas. Among the fatalities, a 71‑year‑old man died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo, in the southern state of Guerrero, according to Governor Evelyn Salgado at a press conference.
summary: Hurricane Simon and Tropical Storm Rachel caused flash flooding and infrastructure damage along Mexico’s Pacific coast, killing at least five people. Among the deaths, a 71‑year‑old man died when a wall collapsed in Chilpancingo, Guerrero, according to Governor Evelyn Salgado.
author: Guardian World

title: Latin American organised crime active in 12 European countries, fueling cocaine surge
content:
A four‑month investigation by the Guardian has uncovered a significant expansion of Latin American organised crime in Europe. The probe found that cartels and factions from Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico and the United States are active in at least 12 European countries, and may operate in up to 16.

The study shows a 471 % increase in the quantity of cocaine seized in Europe between 2014 and 2024, and reports that more local laboratories processing cocaine derivatives have been dismantled during the same period.

The investigation drew on databases, police and intelligence agencies, and interviews with judges, prosecutors and experts from eight countries.
summary: A four‑month Guardian investigation found that Latin American cartels from Colombia, Brazil, Ecuador, Venezuela, Mexico and the US are active in at least 12 European countries, contributing to a 471% rise in cocaine seizures between 2014 and 2024. The investigation also reported that more local laboratories processing cocaine derivatives were dismantled during this period.
author: Guardian World

title: Gaza marks one year since ceasefire as Israeli attacks continue, West Bank oil harvest hit
content:
Palestine weekly reports that Gaza is marking the one‑year anniversary of its ceasefire, yet the period has been marked by an increase in Israeli killings. The outlet notes that Israeli attacks continue to persist a year after the ceasefire was declared.

In the West Bank, settler violence has disrupted the region’s oil harvest, adding further strain to the area’s agricultural activities.
summary: A year after Gaza's ceasefire, Israeli attacks continue. Settler violence has disrupted the West Bank's oil harvest.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Africa's energy wealth contrasted with 560 million lacking electricity
content:
Mapping Africa’s energy wealth reveals that 560 million people on the continent remain without electricity, a figure that accounts for most of the world’s total without power.  

Africa is described as rich in energy resources, yet “hundreds of millions” of Africans still live without electricity, representing the majority of the global population lacking access to power.
summary: Africa is rich in energy. About 560 million Africans still live without electricity, the majority of the world’s total.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ronaldo scores as Al-Nassr win after one‑hour security delay
content:
Al‑Nassr won their AFC Champions League match in Riyadh after the game was delayed for one hour because of a security warning linked to Houthi attacks.  

Cristiano Ronaldo scored for the home side and celebrated by waving a Saudi scarf.
summary: Ronaldo scored and waved a Saudi scarf as Al‑Nassr secured victory. The AFC Champions League match in Riyadh was delayed one hour because of a security warning amid Houthi attacks.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Police detain Cockroach Janta Party leaders at New Delhi protest site
content: Police detained leaders of India’s “cockroach” movement during a protest in New Delhi, according to officials. The volunteers, identified as members of the Cockroach Janta Party, were taken into custody after they entered a popular protest site that authorities had declared off‑limits.
summary: Police detained leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party in New Delhi. They had entered a popular protest site that authorities had declared off-limits.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Yemen escalation raises risk of regional war, but peace still possible
content:
The escalation in Yemen is described as a turning point in the ongoing conflict.  

Analysts note that the risk of a region‑wide war is increasing, but they add that a peaceful arrangement can still be reached if cooler heads prevail.
summary: The escalation in Yemen is raising the risk of a region-wide war. A peaceful arrangement could still be reached if cooler heads prevail.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Former DR Congo President Kabila Joins M23 Rebels in New Coalition
content:
Former Democratic Republic of Congo president Joseph Kabila has aligned himself with the M23 rebel group in a newly announced coalition.  

The alliance has prompted concerns that it could spark additional fighting and lead to a confrontation with the administration of President Félix Tshisekedi.  

Officials and observers warned that the partnership may intensify hostilities between the rebels and the government.
summary: Former DR Congo president Kabila has joined the M23 rebels in a new coalition. The alliance has raised fears of increased fighting and confrontation with President Tshisekedi's government.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Travis Gienger wins fifth pumpkin contest in Half Moon Bay, eyes world record
content:
Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger transported his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California, where he captured the top prize at the town’s annual pumpkin‑growing contest. The victory marks his fifth win in the competition, as noted in the event’s coverage.

Following the latest triumph, Gienger said he is setting his sights on a pumpkin world record.
summary: Horticulture teacher Travis Gienger hauled his pumpkin from Minnesota to Half Moon Bay, California. He won the annual pumpkin contest for the fifth time and said he is aiming for a world record.
author: BBC World

title: India leaders detained after climbing Delhi barricades in protest over election chief
content:
Protesters in central Delhi scaled barricades at a demonstration demanding the resignation of the election chief over revised voter lists.  

Authorities detained leaders who entered the barricaded protest site, referring to them as “cockroach” leaders.  

The incident highlights tension surrounding the changes to the voter rolls and the authorities’ response to the breach of the protest perimeter.
summary: Protesters climbed over barricades in central Delhi. They demanded the election chief resign over revised voter lists, and leaders were detained after entering the barricaded site.
author: BBC World

title: Ship sinks in drone attack off Bulgaria, PM summons Russian ambassador
content:
A ship sank during a new drone attack off the coast of Bulgaria, prompting the prime minister to summon the Russian ambassador for explanations.

The prime minister said two merchant vessels were struck by drones and said he suspects Russia was behind the attacks.
summary: Two merchant ships were hit by drones off Bulgaria, and one sank. Bulgaria's prime minister said he suspects Russia was behind the attacks and summoned the Russian ambassador.
author: BBC World

title: AP releases emergency calls showing delayed response in Christa Pike execution
content:
Emergency calls related to the botched execution of Christa Pike have been released to U.S. media. The recordings were obtained by the Associated Press.

The series of calls reveal that emergency services were delayed in reaching Pike during the incident.
summary: The Associated Press obtained a series of emergency calls related to the botched execution of Christa Pike. The calls reveal that emergency services were delayed in reaching Pike.
author: BBC World

title: One dead, several injured after Six Flags rollercoaster stalls
content:
One person was killed and several others injured after a rollercoaster malfunctioned at a Six Flags amusement park.  

Aerial footage captured after the incident shows the coaster stalled on the track while park staff helped riders off the ride. The park was shown with a stuck rollercoaster and employees assisting guests.
summary: One person was killed and several were injured in a rollercoaster incident at Six Flags. Aerial footage showed the coaster stuck while riders were being helped off.
author: BBC World

title: CRS-35 to launch to ISS with final iROSA arrays and experiments
content: The Commercial Resupply Services-35 (CRS-35) mission is preparing to launch to the International Space Station. The spacecraft will carry the final Integrated Rack Optional Solar Array (iROSA) arrays, along with various experiments and other items. This launch is scheduled to occur shortly after the station completed a crew handover and the return of Crew-12.
summary: The CRS-35 mission is set to launch to the International Space Station. The payload includes the final iROSA arrays, experiments, and other items.
author: NASASpaceFlight

title: Ronaldo’s Al‑Nassr Match Delayed by Missile Alert in Riyadh
content:
Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al-Nassr experienced a one-hour delay in their Asian Champions League match on Monday following a missile alert in Riyadh. The Saudi-led military coalition announced that it had intercepted a missile fired by the Houthis toward the capital city.

The match resumed with Al-Nassr securing a 3-1 victory, during which the Portuguese forward scored a goal. The incident occurred amid a recent series of attacks on Saudi Arabia by the Iran-backed Houthi group, which have targeted oil facilities, tankers, and transport hubs, including lethal strikes on Riyadh’s international airport.
summary: Al‑Nassr’s Asian Champions League match was delayed by an hour after a missile fired by the Houthis was intercepted near Riyadh. Cristiano Ronaldo scored as Al‑Nassr won 3-1.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Coventry secure home win as Mfuni defeats Newcastle
content:
Coventry land long‑awaited home win as Mfuni seals rout of Newcastle

Coventry secured a long‑awaited home victory, climbing out of the relegation zone to 14th place after a second successive win. The result showcased the benefits of the manager’s willingness to balance risk with reward.

The match opened with an early penalty from Jack Rudoni, followed by a quick goal from Sidiki Cherif at the start of the second half. A howitzer from Sven Botman made the score 2‑1, sealing the win.

Frank Lampard noted that the game demonstrates “attack being the best form of defence,” citing the match as a clear example that can be reviewed on Wyscout.
summary: Coventry moved up to 14th place after a second successive win, climbing out of the relegation zone. The victory was sealed by Mfuni in a rout of Newcastle.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Michael Jordan 'Last Dance' jersey sells for record £10.6m
content:
A Michael Jordan jersey from his “Last Dance” season has sold for a record‑setting $14 million, equivalent to £10.6 million, setting a new high for basketball memorabilia.

The sale marks the highest price ever paid for a piece of basketball history, with the jersey’s value surpassing all previous records in the sport.
summary: A Michael Jordan jersey from his 'Last Dance' season sells for $14 million (£10.6 million). It set a record for a piece of basketball memorabilia.
author: BBC Sport

title: Coventry City thrash Newcastle United 4-1 for first home Premier League win in 25 years
content:
Coventry City stunned Newcastle United with a 4‑1 win, securing their first Premier League victory at home in 25 years. The result also marked Coventry’s first home win of the season.

The emphatic victory over Newcastle United gave Coventry a rare triumph in a league where they have struggled to win on their own soil for a quarter of a century.
summary: Coventry City defeated Newcastle United 4-1 in a Premier League match. It was Coventry's first home Premier League win in 25 years.
author: BBC Sport

title: Montana Democratic Chair Shannon O'Brien Resigns, Endorses Independent Senate Candidate
content:
Shannon O’Brien, chair of the Montana Democratic Party, announced her resignation Monday and endorsed independent Senate candidate Seth Bodnar weeks ahead of the November midterm elections.

O’Brien has served as the state party chair since 2025. In an op‑ed for MS NOW, she said the Montana Democratic Party is more divided than ever, citing reasons that she does not elaborate on in the article.

The resignation and endorsement come as Bodnar campaigns for an open seat in the U.S. Senate.
summary: Shannon O'Brien, chair of the Montana Democratic Party, resigned on Monday and endorsed independent Senate candidate Seth Bodnar. She has served as state party chair since 2025 and wrote in an MS NOW op‑ed that the Montana Democratic Party is more divided than ever.
author: The Hill

title: Trump scandals dominate midterm race as Democrats seek to link opponents to president
content:
Scandals surrounding President Trump’s orbit are taking center stage ahead of the midterm elections, as Democrats look for fresh ways to tie their Republican opponents to the president. The focus has shifted to the latest revelations that could impact the political narrative in the run‑up to the polls.

Last week a report surfaced indicating that Trump’s ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, privately solicited cash to pay down her debts ahead of her confirmation hearing. The allegation highlights the growing scrutiny of Trump’s associates and their potential influence on the upcoming electoral contest.
summary: Scandals involving President Trump are taking center stage ahead of the midterm elections as Democrats look for ways to tie their Republican opponents to him. A report last week alleged that Trump’s ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, privately solicited cash to pay down her debts before her confirmation hearing.
author: The Hill

title: Federal agents raid Rep. Ilhan Omar's Washington-area home, Trump critics call it abuse of power
content:
Federal agents raided the Washington area home of Representative Ilhan Omar (D‑Minn.) on Monday, triggering an immediate political firestorm.

Critics of President Trump quickly labeled the raid an abuse of power, arguing it targeted a congresswoman who has been a vigorous opponent of the White House, while conservatives celebrated the action. The Democratic House leadership released a joint statement in response to the raid.
summary: Federal agents raided the Washington-area home of Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) on Monday. Critics of President Trump labeled the raid an abuse of power, while conservatives celebrated.
author: The Hill

title: Roy Cooper leads Michael Whatley by at least 7 points in NC Senate poll
content:
New polling released Monday shows North Carolina Democratic Senate candidate Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley by at least seven points, weeks before the November midterm elections. The Trafalgar Group’s survey reported Cooper at 48.8 percent and Whatley at 40.9 percent.  

The data also indicated that Cooper enjoys larger support across different age demographics. No additional details were provided in the release.
summary: New polling released Monday shows North Carolina Democratic Senate candidate Roy Cooper leading Republican Michael Whatley by at least 7 points. The Trafalgar Group poll gave Cooper 48.8 percent and Whatley 40.9 percent.
author: The Hill

title: Zelensky confronts Trump over Russia diesel deal
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has criticized U.S. President Donald Trump regarding a diesel deal with Russia. The controversy has prompted Kyiv’s allies, including individuals within Trump’s inner circle, to rally around Zelensky in opposition to the agreement.

These supporters are actively pushing back against the diesel deal and Trump’s associated threats to cut off weapons supplies to Ukraine.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized President Trump for a diesel deal with Russia. Kyiv’s allies, including those in President Trump’s circle, are rallying around Zelensky, pushing back against the deal and threats to cut off weapons.
author: The Hill

title: Spicer says he is 'absolutely' concerned about Kansas Senate race
content:
Former White House press secretary Sean Spicer stated on Monday that he is “absolutely” concerned about the potential for Republicans to lose the Kansas Senate race. Election handicappers have indicated that the seat, currently held by a Republican, could flip in favor of the Democrats.

The comments were made during an interview on NewsNation’s “The Hill,” where host Blake Burman asked Spicer if he worried about Republicans losing the Kansas Senate seat.
summary: Former White House press secretary Sean Spicer stated on Monday that he is "absolutely" concerned about Republicans losing the Kansas Senate race. Election handicappers indicate the seat could flip in favor of the Democrats.
author: The Hill

title: Trump Criticizes Minnesota and Rep. Ilhan Omar During Ohio Campaign Stop
content:
President Trump repeatedly criticized Minnesota and Representative Ilhan Omar during a campaign stop in Ohio on Monday night, where he was stumping for Republican candidates ahead of the midterms. During the event, the President highlighted recent events in the state to bolster his message to supporters.

The remarks came on the same day that federal agents searched the home of Rep. Omar, a Somali-born American citizen, as part of a federal criminal investigation. Trump referenced these developments, stating, “Just look at what’s happening in the once great…”
summary: President Trump repeatedly mentioned Minnesota and Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minn.) while stumping for Republicans in Ohio ahead of the midterms. Federal agents searched Omar's home on Monday as part of a federal criminal investigation into her, a Somali-born American citizen.
author: The Hill

title: Government spent $10 million on pro-Trump ads after Trump said super PAC would fund
content: Nearly $22 million in taxpayer funds has been spent to air pro-Trump advertisements. According to the report, nearly half of this amount was spent after President Trump promised to fund what the White House describes as public service announcements through his super PAC.
summary: Nearly $22 million in taxpayers funds has been spent to air the ads. Nearly half was spent after Trump promised to fund what the White House calls public service announcements through his super PAC.
author: NPR Politics

title: Katie Zacharia Named New White House Press Secretary, Trump Fan
content:
Katie Zacharia is set to become the White House press secretary, a role that will make her the chief spokesperson for the president. Her appointment follows a career in which she worked for one of Donald Trump’s companies and gained prominence by appearing on conservative-leaning talk shows.

Zacharia has also been noted for amplifying right-wing conspiracy theories. The new press secretary is described as a "devoted fan" of Trump and the MAGA movement.
summary: Katie Zacharia, a devoted fan of Trump and MAGA, has been named the president's chief spokesperson. She previously worked for one of Trump's companies, appeared on conservative-leaning talk shows, and amplified right-wing conspiracy theories.
author: NPR Politics

title: Cardiac Rehab Availability Lags Behind Rising Global Cardiovascular Disease
content: A new study by York University researchers indicates that the global availability of cardiac rehabilitation programs has not increased over the past decade, despite a rising incidence of cardiovascular disease (CVD). The findings highlight a gap in healthcare resources, as evidence shows that these programs improve outcomes for individuals living with CVD.
summary: A new York University study finds that cardiac rehabilitation program availability has not increased worldwide over the past decade, despite rising cardiovascular disease (CVD) incidence. The study notes that cardiac rehab programs improve outcomes for people living with CVD.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Menopause involves abrupt body-wide physiological changes, study finds
content:
Research published in Nature Medicine indicates that the final menstrual period is preceded by abrupt, "cliff-like" biological changes across multiple body systems. The study suggests that menopause-related physiological changes occur over a shorter time frame than previously believed.

Some of these changes show early signs more than a decade before the final menstrual period. The findings advance the understanding of how early these physiological shifts can be detected.
summary: Research published in Nature Medicine indicates that the final menstrual period is preceded by abrupt biological changes across multiple body systems. Some of these changes show early signs more than a decade before menopause, suggesting the process occurs over a shorter time frame than previously thought.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UK professor says European ADHD rise reflects diagnosis changes
content:
ADHD has dominated headlines recently, prompting debate over whether the apparent increase in cases reflects a true rise or simply heightened awareness and diagnostic practices.  

Professor Anita Thapar, preparing a presentation for Europe’s main clinical neuroscience conference, noted that the perceived surge in ADHD diagnoses across the continent appears to stem mainly from changes in awareness and diagnostic criteria. She added that evidence points to ADHD still being underdiagnosed in several countries.  

These findings suggest that while more cases are being identified, the underlying prevalence may not have changed significantly, and gaps in diagnosis remain in some European regions.
summary: Professor Anita Thapar stated that the rise in ADHD cases across Europe appears mainly due to changes in awareness and diagnosis. She noted that growing evidence suggests ADHD remains underdiagnosed in some countries.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Females with autoimmune diseases likely misdiagnosed as psychiatric conditions than males
content: A study involving more than 6,600 patients found that females with autoimmune diseases are significantly more likely than males to have their conditions misdiagnosed as psychiatric or psychosomatic issues. The research highlights a disparity in how these medical conditions are identified and treated based on gender.
summary: A study of more than 6,600 patients found that females with autoimmune diseases are significantly more likely than males to have their condition misdiagnosed as a psychiatric or psychosomatic condition. The study highlights a gender disparity in the diagnosis of autoimmune diseases.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Marital status changes linked to higher risk of alcohol problems
content:
A study published in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research indicates that individuals experiencing mixed marital transitions or those who have never been married may face a higher likelihood of developing alcohol-related problems compared to those with stable marital statuses. The research specifically identifies people in early midlife going through mixed marital transitions and individuals who remain unmarried into late life as being particularly vulnerable to alcohol use issues.

These findings underscore the connection between romantic relationships and alcohol consumption. The study suggests that further evaluation is needed for interventions tailored to specific ages, sexes, and life stages to help mitigate the risk of problematic alcohol use among people navigating marital transitions.
summary: A study in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research found that people who have experienced mixed marital transitions or who have never been married are more likely to have alcohol-related problems than those with stable marital status. The research highlights the need for interventions tailored to age, sex, and life stage to reduce problematic alcohol use among individuals undergoing marital transitions.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Cochrane review finds insufficient evidence that medical cannabis helps insomnia
content: A new Cochrane review concludes that current evidence is too uncertain to determine whether medical cannabis improves sleep or daytime functioning in individuals with insomnia. The review found insufficient data to support the use of medical cannabis for this condition.
summary: A new Cochrane review finds that existing evidence is too uncertain to determine whether medical cannabis improves sleep or daytime functioning in people with insomnia. The review concludes that the evidence is insufficient to support medical cannabis as a treatment for insomnia.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Choline supplementation in young children with fetal alcohol spectrum disorder  can have durable developmental benefits
content:
Children with prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) may benefit from a simple nutritional intervention, according to a new study. Researchers found that supplemental choline, an essential nutrient, produced long‑lasting cognitive gains in young children affected by PAE.

The study suggests that choline supplementation could become a scalable treatment for neurodevelopmental differences that currently have few options. Fetal alcohol spectrum disorder (FASD) is an umbrella term for several diagnoses that affect 1%–5% of the global population and can involve physical, cognitive and behavioral deficits and challenges.
summary: Children affected by prenatal alcohol exposure (PAE) experience long-lasting cognitive gains after treatment with supplemental choline, an essential nutrient, a new study suggests. The findings point to a potentially scalable intervention for neurodevelopmental differences that currently have few treatment options.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Publicly Owned Rail Popular, But Timeliness in Question
content:
Publicly owned rail remains popular, but questions persist about its ability to keep trains on schedule. The system’s popularity does not guarantee punctuality, according to recent discussions.

Experts warn that meeting travellers' expectations could be challenging, highlighting potential gaps between public demand and service reliability.
summary: Experts warn that meeting travellers' expectations could be challenging. The article questions whether publicly owned rail is delivering on-time trains.
author: BBC Business

title: Heating Oil Customers Face Soaring Bills Despite Government Regulation Promise
content: Heating oil customers are facing soaring bills, but the government has promised improved regulation of the sector. The promise comes amid concerns over rising costs for consumers who rely on heating oil for winter heating. No further details on the specific regulatory measures were provided.
summary: Heating oil customers are facing soaring bills. The government has promised better regulation of the sector.
author: BBC Business

title: Social media clipper earns £120,000 a year making videos go viral
content:
I earn £120,000 a year making social media videos go viral.  

The earnings come from producing short, vertical videos that appear on platforms such as Instagram and TikTok.  

Social media “clippers” are the creators who produce these videos, which are designed to capture viewers’ attention on the likes of Instagram and TikTok.
summary: The clipper earns £120,000 per year by creating short, vertical videos that go viral on social media. These videos appear on platforms such as Instagram and TikTok.
author: BBC Business

title: Nanostructure-assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment
content:
Nanostructure‑assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment

Parkinson's disease (PD) is one of the most common neurological disorders associated with later life, and its prevalence rises sharply with age. It affects the brain systems that control movement, often causing tremor, stiffness, slowness and problems with balance, all of which can reduce independence and quality of life in older adults. The condition is mainly linked to the gradual loss of dopamine‑producing nerve cells.
summary: Nanostructure-assisted ultrasound shows potential for Parkinson's treatment. Parkinson's disease is a common neurological disorder that causes tremor, stiffness, slowness and balance problems because of the gradual loss of dopamine-producing nerve cells.

content:

The report details a broad spectrum of threats that impacted electoral processes, including violence, misinformation, and disinformation. It also identifies electoral management malfunctions, cyberattacks, and natural hazards as key factors undermining the integrity of elections.  

The findings highlight the persistent pressures faced by electoral systems across the globe during the 2025 election cycle.

content:

The researchers note that, in the future, this system could be adapted to slow cellular aging and enhance cancer therapies. Additionally, the finding offers insight into an ancient evolutionary event that may have set the stage for the emergence of higher organisms.

title: Magnetic sculpting transforms single-source fields into predetermined shapes with mathematical precision
content:
Magnetic fields, though invisible, are crucial in technologies such as MRI scanners, particle accelerators, atomic clocks, and emerging quantum computers. Each application demands magnetic fields with precise shapes and properties.

Creating these tailored fields currently requires researchers and engineers to design specialized, carefully optimized magnets or large systems of coils for each individual application. This process is complex and resource-intensive.
summary: Magnetic fields are invisible yet essential components in technologies ranging from MRI scanners and particle accelerators to atomic clocks and future quantum computers. Each of these applications requires magnetic fields with specific shapes and properties.

content:

The discovery came after centuries of mining had erased much of the archaeological record, allowing researchers to trace the industry’s origins.  

The findings were published in the journal Antiquity.

content:
Recent research has revealed a deep connection between gravity and quantum information, showing that the shape of spacetime can be traced back to the way information is stored in quantum fields. The study derives Einstein’s equations from principles of quantum information, suggesting that gravitational dynamics may emerge from underlying informational structures.

The work indicates that the geometry of spacetime is not an independent backdrop but is determined by the distribution and storage of quantum information within fields. This finding links the fundamental laws of gravity to the informational content of quantum systems.

title: Chatham House analyst says Moscow is playing with Washington over diesel export deal
content:
President Donald Trump’s envoys told Ukrainian officials on Friday that a proposed deal to permit Russian diesel exports is intended to coax Russia back into negotiations after earlier attempts to launch sustained talks to end the war failed, three people familiar with the meeting said, according to Reuters.  

In a separate interview, FRANCE 24’s Sharon Gaffney spoke with Grégoire Roos, director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House. Roos said, “It’s clear that Moscow is just playing with Washington because Vladimir Putin knows that Donald Trump lives on borrowed time.”  

Both remarks highlight ongoing diplomatic efforts and differing assessments of Moscow’s strategy toward the United States.
summary: President Donald Trump's envoys told Ukrainian officials that a deal to allow Russian diesel exports is meant to draw Russia back to negotiations after earlier attempts failed. Grégoire Roos, director of the Europe and Russia and Eurasia Programmes at Chatham House, said Moscow is playing with Washington because Vladimir Putin knows Donald Trump lives on borrowed time.

content:
Bolivia’s attorney general has opened an investigation into former president Evo Morales, alleging that he was involved in the 2009 murder and torture of European citizens. The probe focuses on a police raid on a hotel in Santa Cruz that resulted in the deaths of three Europeans.

During the raid, police shot dead Eduardo Rózsa Flores, a Bolivian‑Croatian, Michael Dwyer, an Irishman, and Árpád Magyarosi, a Hungarian‑Romanian. The investigation also alleges that two other European individuals were tortured in connection with the same incident.

The attorney general’s announcement marks a formal inquiry into Morales’s alleged ties to the 2009 killings and related abuses.

The document includes recommendations aimed at improving the sustainability of the sport. A final version of the report is expected to be released in the spring, following an eight-week public consultation period that begins this week.
summary: The Independent Football Regulator (IFR) will recommend that clubs introduce greater cost controls in its State of the Game report. content:
Matt Renshaw’s return to the Australian Test side was marked by a dramatic performance in the first Test against South Africa in Durban. After a brief comeback innings of eight runs, he travelled to South Africa where his role as opener shifted to batting fifth.

Over the first two days of the match Renshaw scored an impressive 190, helping to rescue Australia from a precarious position. On the fourth day he added another 82, top‑scoring again as Australia declared at 316 for six. The Australians set South Africa 421 runs to win.

Australia’s bowlers closed the game with four wickets for 102, leaving South Africa reeling. Aiden Markram, who has scored 45, is expected to be the main obstacle to an Australian series lead on the final day.
summary: Matt Renshaw scored 190 in the first two days of the first Test in Durban and top scored again with 82 on the fourth day. Australia set South Africa 421 to win and took four wickets for 102 by the close, with Aiden Markram on 45 as the main obstacle to an Australian series lead.

title: Christian Horner Reflects on Pain of Being Sacked After 20 Years at Red Bull
content:
Christian Horner, the 52‑year‑old team principal who led Red Bull Racing to become an F1 powerhouse over two decades, has spoken publicly about the pain he felt after being sacked. He described the experience as a source of panic attacks and has questioned his purpose in life following the abrupt end to his tenure.

The interview was conducted on an autumn morning in Highgate, where Horner was joined by his wife, Geri Halliwell‑Horner, a former Spice Girl. Halliwell‑Horner greeted the interviewer with a cheerful hug and performed an imitation of a South African accent, referencing her former headteacher at Watford Girls School.

During the conversation, the couple discussed their two daughters, who had attended Halliwell‑Horner’s school, and noted that one of the school’s history textbooks contained her name on an inside page. Halliwell‑Horner also spoke about the gritty nature of old Watford, grammar school education, and Nelson Mandela.
summary: Christian Horner, 52, reflects on the pain of being sacked after two decades turning Red Bull into an F1 powerhouse. He is questioning his purpose in life and dealing with panic attacks.

content:
The United Nations regulator has mandated that cookstove projects must now account for the risk of future forest loss. This new requirement compels these initiatives to protect against the possibility that the trees they save may be destroyed later.

This regulatory change marks the first time such a provision has been implemented for cookstove projects. The decision was made despite lobbying efforts aimed at securing an exemption from these new protections.

title: Rescued turtles return to Gingham water hole after NSW government cut flows
content:
Ten broad-shelled turtles and three Murray River turtles have been released back into the Gingham water hole in New South Wales’ Gwydir region. The freshwater turtles were previously rescued from the dried-up water hole after the state government halted environmental water to the area.

The cessation of water flows followed a complaint from a private landholder, an action that reportedly led to the deaths of wildlife and sheep.
summary: Ten broad-shelled turtles and three Murray River turtles were released back into the Gingham water hole in western New South Wales. title: Super El Niño Threatens Food System; Farms Can Prepare
content:
Liz Carlisle, an associate professor of Environmental Studies at UC Santa Barbara, highlights the threat that a potentially record-breaking El Niño poses to the global food system. While forecasters warn that Central and South America, the Caribbean, and southern Africa will face the most severe impacts, Carlisle notes that the United States could still experience significant crop losses due to severe weather.

To mitigate these risks, Carlisle advocates for agricultural practices that protect soil amid potential flooding, such as planting cover crops or perennial plants. She emphasizes that Congress must take action to protect these regenerative farming methods. Carlisle is the author of Healing Grounds: Climate, Justice, and the Deep Roots of Regenerative Farming and co-editor of Living Roots: The Promise of Perennial Foods.
summary: Forecasters warn that this year's El Niño could become the strongest on record, raising concerns about its impact on agriculture and food security. Farmers can protect soil by planting cover crops or perennial plants, but Congress must act to safeguard these practices.

title: Judge Halts Tree Cutting at East Potomac Golf Course Amid Trump Expansion Plans
content:

The judge granted the temporary stay while she reviews an emergency request from plaintiffs who argue that construction activities are proceeding despite a pending legal challenge.

title: Early gut microbes aid newborn immune system against infections, mouse studies show
content:
New research using mouse experiments indicates that early gut microbes assist the newborn immune system in combating deadly infections. While infants are born with a baseline level of immunity, they possess fewer defensive mechanisms than adults to fight diseases.

The developing immune system relies on exposure to pathogens to build its repertoire, a process that simultaneously leaves babies vulnerable to infection because many immune defenses are still maturing.
summary: Mouse experiments suggest that early gut microbes help the newborn immune system fight deadly infections. Newborns have limited immune tools compared to adults, making them vulnerable to infection despite some innate immunity.

content:
Researchers at the University of Colorado Anschutz and Pacific Northwest National Laboratory have identified a potential mechanism linking a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer's disease to brain immune cell function. The study suggests that a protein associated with the disease can alter how these immune cells process fat and trigger inflammation.

This finding offers a new clue into why certain individuals are more susceptible to developing Alzheimer's. By modifying the activity of brain immune cells, the protein may help explain how established genetic risks influence brain health and disease progression.

title: Study links rising brain cancer risk to increased radon exposure
content:
A recent study has linked brain cancer risk to higher levels of radon exposure. The research involved long‑term tracking of nearly 160,000 people from across the United States.

The analysis found that as individuals’ exposure to radon increased, so did their risk of developing brain cancer. The findings suggest a direct correlation between elevated radon concentrations and brain cancer incidence.

title: Water Shape at Tau Hotspot Drives Dementia-Linked Clumping
content:
Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal dementia are classified as neurodegenerative tauopathies, conditions in which tau proteins within the brain misfold and result in cognitive decline. The specific mechanism by which misfolded tau recruits other healthy tau proteins to misfold and clump has previously remained unclear.

Recent research indicates that the shape of water at a key tau hotspot plays a role in driving this dementia-linked clumping process.
summary: The study shows that the shape of water at a key tau hotspot helps drive the clumping of tau proteins, which is linked to diseases such as Alzheimer's and frontotemporal dementia. This finding explains how misfolded tau can recruit healthy tau to misfold and aggregate, leading to cognitive decline.

title: Study Finds Long‑Term Alcohol Use and Mental Health Patterns Vary After Disasters
content:
A recent study published in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research examined how exposure to disasters shapes long‑term mental health and alcohol use. Researchers found that individuals who experienced disasters displayed distinct trajectories of alcohol consumption and mental health outcomes that were interrelated.

The analysis revealed that both individual differences and the specific type of disaster influenced these patterns. The findings underscore the persistent mental and behavioral health challenges faced by disaster survivors.

The study highlights the need for interventions that are tailored to each survivor’s mental health profile in order to prevent problem drinking.
summary: The study, published in Alcohol: Clinical and Experimental Research, found that people exposed to disasters show different long‑term patterns of alcohol use and mental health. It highlights the need for interventions tailored to individuals' mental health profiles to prevent problem drinking.

title: Broad Institute study shows drug combo reducing oxygen improves Parkinson's symptoms in mice
content: Broad Institute researchers have reported that a combination of two small-molecule chemicals that reduce oxygen delivery to cells improved symptoms of neurodegeneration in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease. This new study builds on prior findings by the scientists, who had previously identified that excess oxygen in the brain is associated with neuronal death in Parkinson's disease. Their earlier research also indicated that reducing the oxygen levels inhaled by mice could help reverse disease symptoms.
summary: Broad Institute researchers found that two small-molecule chemicals that reduce oxygen delivery to cells improved symptoms of neurodegeneration in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease. The study builds on earlier findings that excess oxygen in the brain is linked to neuronal death and that reducing the oxygen that mice breathe could help reverse symptoms.

content:

The study analyzed blood and spinal fluid samples from 200 individuals to investigate this connection.
summary: Johns Hopkins Medicine researchers conducted a preliminary study using blood and spinal fluid samples from 200 people. They found evidence that a protein involved in blood pressure regulation may serve as a marker for treatment-resistant schizophrenia and other psychoses.

content:

title: Hall and Woodford Awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics for Crisis‑Smoothing Models
content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in economics was awarded to two U.S. economists for developing models that help central bankers and finance ministers stabilize their economies.

Robert Hall of Stanford University, California, and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, New York, were recognized for creating the “microeconomic foundations of macroeconomic stabilisation.” Their work provides policymakers with tools to smooth out the peaks and troughs of their economies, thereby avoiding long recessions and runaway inflation.
summary: Robert Hall of Stanford University, California, and Michael Woodford of Columbia University, New York, received the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics for developing models that help central bankers and finance ministers stabilise their economies. title: Primordial helium confirms Big Bang composition
content:
In the early moments of the Big Bang, hydrogen and helium were the primary elements forged, with the early universe consisting of approximately three parts hydrogen to one part helium. While tiny traces of light elements like lithium were also produced, they were not of significant consequence.

All heavier elements, including the oxygen in human lungs and the iron in blood, were created later through astrophysical processes. These elements were fused in stars, formed in supernovae, or scattered by collisions between neutron stars.

In the present cosmos, heavier elements are so rare that astronomers collectively classify them as metals.
summary: In the early moments of the Big Bang, hydrogen and helium were forged, with a ratio of about three parts hydrogen to one part helium, and tiny traces of lithium were also produced. Heavier elements such as oxygen and iron were later created in stars, supernovae, and neutron star collisions.

title: UCLA study links 2024 record rainfall to El Niño and global warming
content:
A new study from UCLA has found that the 2024 El Niño has already set a record for extreme rainfall, with 40 % of the increase linked to global warming. The research notes that strong El Niños have occurred only four times in as many decades, yet the 2024 event is already showing signs of a sequel.

The UCLA team’s analysis indicates that the unprecedented rainfall is tied to the warming climate, and that the current atmospheric conditions are favorable for another intense El Niño. The study highlights that the 2024 event broke the previous record for extreme rainfall associated with El Niño.

These findings suggest that the climate system is primed for a repeat of the 2024 rainfall pattern, underscoring the growing impact of global warming on El Niño events.
summary: UCLA research found that 2024 broke the record for extreme rainfall, with 40% of the increase tied to global warming. The study notes that strong El Niños have occurred only four times in as many decades and that conditions are ripe for a repeat.

title: Audit staffing structure improves audit outcomes, study finds
content:
New research from the University at Buffalo School of Management indicates that the staffing structure of an audit office significantly influences audit outcomes. The study highlights the distinct roles within audit firms, where partners oversee audits and client relationships, managers supervise teams and projects, and staff handle much of the day-to-day work.

The findings suggest that audit quality improves when a higher number of audit partners and managers are actively involved in supervising and reviewing audit engagements.
summary: Audit firms use partners, managers, and staff in a tiered structure. Research from the University at Buffalo School of Management shows that greater partner and manager involvement improves audit quality.

title: Tiny fossils reveal a missing chapter of ocean life after Snowball Earth
content: A rare collection of micro- and macro-fossils discovered in a roadside outcrop in South China provides insight into marine life following one of Earth's most extreme ice ages. The assemblage includes distinct structures such as thin ribbons, branching shapes, and a tiny balloon on a stalk. These findings offer a glimpse into the biological history of the oceans during this period.
summary: A rare assemblage of micro- and macro-fossils was found in a roadside outcrop in South China. The fossils, which include thin ribbons, branching shapes, and a tiny balloon on a stalk, provide evidence of marine life after the Snowball Earth ice age.

title: Neuroscientists and philosophers debate Claude's global workspace on luxury yacht
content:
A debate about artificial intelligence and consciousness recently took place on a luxury yacht. The discussion brought together neuroscientists and philosophers to examine whether the chatbot Claude might exhibit a form of consciousness.

The conversation centered on a leading theory of consciousness that describes experience as information flowing through a global workspace in the mind. Participants explored whether similar patterns could be detected in Claude’s internal processes.

The debate highlighted the possibility that AI systems like Claude might process information in a way that mirrors the global workspace model, raising questions about the emergence of consciousness in artificial agents.
summary: A leading theory of consciousness posits experience as information flowing through a global workspace in the mind. Neuroscientists and philosophers debated signs of a similar workspace in the chatbot Claude while on a luxury yacht.

title: Russia’s silence on lab worker’s plague death raises pandemic preparedness concerns
content:

While scientists typically focus on technical challenges such as identifying pathogens and developing vaccines, Sridhar emphasizes that political factors significantly impact global health security.

The recent incident involving a suspected pneumonic plague case in Russia has generated global headlines, a development Sridhar notes was unpredictable. Although the World Health Organization (WHO) monitors thousands of potential disease signals monthly, the specific circumstances of this case are considered unusual due to the lack of transparency from Russian authorities. Sridhar points to ongoing concerns about biological weapons research as a key factor in the heightened attention surrounding the incident.
summary: Russia has not provided information about the death of a lab worker suspected of having pneumonic plague. The lack of transparency has raised concerns about pandemic preparedness and potential biological weapons research.

title: NASA Sends Health Research to ISS on SpaceX CRS-35 Mission
content:
NASA’s SpaceX CRS‑35 mission will carry a suite of health‑research experiments to the International Space Station. The payload focuses on human and plant health as well as drug‑resistant organisms.

The experiments will be launched aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services flight from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The mission is part of NASA’s effort to advance research that benefits life on Earth and supports future exploration.

The research is intended to support astronaut health during long‑duration missions.
summary: NASA experiments on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida. The research supports astronaut health during long‑duration missions and benefits life on Earth and future exploration.
