title: America and China lead new lunar race as nations vie for Moon
content:
The article opens with the headline “Mars may be a hellhole, but the moon is not far behind,” suggesting a comparison between the two celestial bodies. The text that follows, however, focuses on the current competition for lunar exploration.

It describes the present effort as the “second space race,” noting that the earlier one involved the Soviet Union and the United States competing to plant flags. The new race is framed as a sprint to the lunar surface between America and China, with other nations also involved.
summary: The competition is being called a second space race. Now it’s a sprint to the lunar surface between America and China, alongside a host of friendly and rival nations.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: AlterMe Review: Smart Ring Aids Habits, Genetic Insights Disappoint
content:
AlterMe Review: Fitness Built Around My DNA

A recent review of AlterMe’s smart ring and accompanying fitness app reports that the user spent six months using the device and the app. The review states that the experience helped the user build better habits. However, the reviewer notes that the genetic insights provided by the service were less revealing than expected.
summary: I used AlterMe’s smart ring and fitness app for six months. The device helped me build better habits, but the genetic insights were less revealing than I’d hoped.
author: Wired

title: Feds Get Warrants to Use Fake Cell Towers to Hunt Don Lemon’s Producer
content:
Federal investigators obtained warrants to deploy fake cell towers in an effort to locate Don Lemon’s producer.  

In addition, investigators sought permission to use an invasive surveillance tool known as cell‑site simulators against journalist Georgia Fort and a Minnesota state Senate candidate.
summary: Feds obtained warrants to use fake cell towers to locate Don Lemon’s producer. Investigators also sought permission to use cell-site simulators against journalist Georgia Fort and a Minnesota state Senate candidate.
author: Wired

title: Apple Adds Indigenous Languages to iPhone Keyboard to Preserve Endangered Languages
content:
Apple is adding Indigenous languages to the iPhone keyboard as part of an effort to preserve endangered languages.  

The company is working directly with Indigenous communities to incorporate these languages into the device’s typing options, meeting the next generation where they type.  

The initiative aims to help save endangered languages.
summary: Apple is adding Indigenous languages to the iPhone keyboard to help preserve endangered languages. The company is collaborating with Indigenous communities to provide language options for the next generation.
author: Wired

title: Google Fitbit Edge: $179 Tracker with Pixel Watch Smarts, OLED Screen, Week-Long Battery
content:
Google has announced the Fitbit Edge, a new fitness tracker priced at $179. The device is positioned as a budget-friendly alternative to Google’s Pixel Watch.

Key features of the Edge include “Pixel Watch smarts,” a week‑long battery life, and an OLED display.
summary: The new Google Fitbit Edge tracker costs $179. It includes Pixel Watch smarts, a week-long battery life, and an OLED screen.
author: Wired

title: Documentary ‘The Sixty-Year Mission’ Highlights Star Trek’s Forward-Thinking Views
content:
A new documentary titled “The Sixty-Year Mission” examines the lasting impact of the Star Trek franchise. The film highlights how the series’ stances on issues ranging from race to artificial intelligence were ahead of their time.

By chronicling these pioneering perspectives, the documentary aims to introduce the legacy of Star Trek to a new generation of viewers.
summary: The documentary ‘The Sixty-Year Mission’ examines Star Trek’s legacy for a new generation. It shows how the series’ positions on race and artificial intelligence were ahead of their time.
author: Wired

title: First simulation shows geopolitics driving solar geoengineering arms race
content:
A first‑of‑its‑kind simulation examined the geopolitical dynamics of solar geoengineering, a technique that could “buy humanity time” against climate change.  

The model showed how the practice of dimming the sun might also spark a dangerous new arms race, highlighting the risks when geopolitics drives the technology.  

The findings suggest that while solar geoengineering offers potential climate benefits, its deployment could exacerbate international tensions.
summary: Solar geoengineering could buy humanity time against climate change or trigger a dangerous new arms race. A first‑of‑its‑kind simulation offered a glimpse of what happens when geopolitics takes the wheel.
author: Wired

title: Meta launches Muse Wonder, its largest AI model rivaling top systems
content:
Meta has unveiled its largest artificial‑intelligence model, branded Muse Wonder, positioning the company once again at the forefront of AI development.  

The Muse Wonder system is described as rivaling the world’s best AI models, while incorporating new safety mechanisms designed to keep agents from “going off the rails.”  

The announcement signals Meta’s renewed focus on advancing large‑scale AI capabilities with built‑in safeguards.
summary: Meta has introduced Muse Wonder, its biggest AI model. The model rivals the world’s best and includes new features to keep agents from going off the rails.
author: Wired

title: Elon Musk boasts Grok Lego Star Wars haul, then X users prank him
content: Elon Musk boasted on X about his recent acquisition of a Grok LEGO Star Wars collection. Shortly after, other users on the platform responded with a jab, writing, “Musk, we find your lack of security disturbing.” The exchange highlighted a brief online back‑and‑forth between the billionaire and X users. No further details were provided.
summary: Elon Musk bragged about his Grok Lego Star Wars collection. X users punked him, saying “Musk, we find your lack of security disturbing.”
author: Wired

title: CMF launches first portable Bluetooth speakers with milk‑carton look
content:
CMF has introduced its first portable Bluetooth speakers, the CMF Speaker Series, marking the budget‑focused brand’s entry into wireless audio. The speakers are being launched as Nothing, the company that created CMF, prepares to spin the brand off into an India‑based standalone subsidiary.

The new devices are positioned as affordable options with distinctive designs and bright colour choices, a pattern also seen in CMF’s Headphone Pro that debuted a year earlier. While the company does not claim a dairy‑aisle inspiration, the speakers’ shape has drawn comparisons to electronic milk cartons.

Two versions of the CMF Speaker Series are available, though further specifications were not detailed in the source.
summary: The CMF Speaker Series are the first portable Bluetooth speakers from CMF, a budget‑focused brand created by Nothing that is being spun off into an India‑based subsidiary. They are priced for affordability, come in bright color options and feature a design that resembles electronic milk cartons.
author: The Verge

title: OnePlus 16 launches in China as first flagship after US, Europe exit
content:
OnePlus unveiled its OnePlus 16 in China, the first flagship the company has released since pulling out of the United States and European markets earlier this summer.  

The handset is built around a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, offers up to 1 TB of storage with 16 GB of RAM, and is powered by a 9,000 mAh silicon‑carbon battery—one of the largest seen in an Android flagship. It supports 100 W wired and 50 W wireless charging and features a 185 Hz OLED display, the first such panel on a OnePlus device.  

The Verge describes the OnePlus 16 as the company’s most interesting phone in years.
summary: The OnePlus 16 was launched in China, marking the company's first flagship phone since it quit the US and European markets this summer. It is equipped with a Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, up to 1 TB of storage, 16 GB of RAM, a 9,000 mAh silicon‑carbon battery with 100 W wired and 50 W wireless charging, and a 185 Hz OLED display.
author: The Verge

title: No Man’s Sky launches on iPhone and iPad on Oct. 28
content:
Hello Games announced that its long‑running sci‑fi exploration title No Man’s Sky will launch on iOS, with versions for both iPhone and iPad slated for release on October 28.

In a blog post, Hello Games founder Sean Murray said the mobile version delivers “the full No Man’s Sky experience,” emphasizing that it is not a “Lite” edition. The port will incorporate all of the game’s post‑launch updates, including the Voyagers expansion released last year.

The only major features omitted from the iOS version are multiplayer and an additional, unspecified component.
summary: Hello Games announced that the full No Man’s Sky experience will be released for iOS on iPhone and iPad on October 28. The mobile version includes all post‑launch updates such as the Voyagers expansion, with multiplayer omitted.
author: The Verge

title: Android praised and criticized in review of Asus and HP Googlebooks laptops
content:
A reviewer who tested two Android‑powered “Googlebooks” — an Asus model and an HP model — said the devices deliver a mixed experience. During the first week of use, the reviewer described the laptops as “rocky” but noted a gradual improvement in their perception of the machines.

Positive moments were attributed to Android’s integration, including access to native versions of useful apps and the ability to view phone notifications directly from the laptop’s user interface. However, the reviewer also highlighted several shortcomings: phone connectivity was described as “flaky,” app casting was “awkward,” and file‑sharing was “flat‑out broken.” Additional complaints were mentioned regarding the limitations of native Android apps on the devices.

The full review appears on The Verge.
summary: The reviewer tested two Android-powered Googlebooks laptops, an Asus model and an HP model, during a first week of use. They said Android improved app access and phone notifications but suffered flaky phone connectivity, awkward app casting and broken file‑sharing.
author: The Verge

title: Mechanism launches $49 Basecase, first Switch 2 snap‑on shell with Lego‑compatible rear
content:
Mechanism has released its first case for the Nintendo Switch 2, the $49 Basecase, a snap‑on shell that adds protection and comfort to the handheld console. The case features 3D‑printed grips and a rear plate that offers unofficial compatibility with LEGO blocks and minifigures, and it integrates with Mechanism’s existing modular mount system.

The new Basecase builds on the company’s $19 Basegrip, which already allows the Switch 2 to be mounted to walls, a Gaming Pillow, a monitor arm and other surfaces. According to the announcement, the shell preserves the full range of the Switch 2’s kickstand and provides access to all of the console’s ports while making the Joy‑Con controllers more comfortable to use. The launch comes after a period in which most companies have slowed the release of new Switch 2 cases.
summary: The $49 Basecase from Mechanism is a snap‑on shell for the Switch 2 that adds a rear plate compatible with Lego blocks and minifigs. It expands the company’s modular lineup, protecting the console, improving Joy‑Con comfort, and allowing full kickstand range and mount options such as the $19 Basegrip.
author: The Verge

title: Yandex outage linked to drop in bot traffic, but not disinformation farms
content:
Multiple Ukrainian drone strikes over the past week have knocked Russian data centers offline, leading to a reported drop in overall online bot traffic. A chart based on Cloudflare data that has been shared on social media shows a sharp decline in bot traffic after the attacks on Yandex servers, the technology firm often described as “Russia’s Google.”  

Analysts note that while the chart has prompted speculation that the reduction reflects a slowdown in bot farms that disseminate disinformation, conspiracy theories and other harmful content, the decline likely pertains to a different category of automated activity. The source suggests the outage did not “blitz” the type of Russian bots most people associate with coordinated misinformation campaigns.  

The story, originally reported by The Verge, highlights the distinction between general bot traffic reductions caused by infrastructure damage and targeted disinformation operations.
summary: Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data centers have taken Yandex servers offline and coincided with a sharp decline in bot traffic reported by Cloudflare data. Analysts say the reduction likely reflects non‑disinformation bot activity rather than the troll farms that push harmful content.
author: The Verge

title: Elon Musk donates at least $276 million to Republican groups for midterm efforts
content:
Elon Musk has contributed at least $276 million to Republican groups since July, according to a report by The New York Times, making him the party’s top known donor and the largest established midterm donor.  

Of the total, $158 million has been directed to the Senate Leadership Fund, the primary super PAC working to secure and maintain a Republican Senate majority and to defend the party’s Senate seat in Texas, a state that houses a major portion of Musk’s business interests.  

Musk has also given more than $76 million to America PAC, a super PAC he founded in 2024 that conducts canvassing efforts.  

The donations position Musk as a leading financial backer of Republican midterm campaigns.
summary: Elon Musk has handed out at least $276 million to Republican groups since July, according to The New York Times, making him the party’s top known donor and the biggest established midterm donor. $158 million of the donations went to the Senate Leadership Fund and more than $76 million went to America PAC, a super PAC Musk founded in 2024.
author: The Verge

title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full AI models for subscribers
content:
Meta announced the launch of two new artificial‑intelligence models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, expanding its recent AI portfolio that includes the Muse Spark model and the Muse agent. The company said the new models are intended to compete “toe‑to‑toe with the industry’s best.”

Both models are available to Muse Code subscribers as of today, and Muse Wonder can also be accessed through the Meta Model API, Meta said. The firm added that it plans to eventually power its Muse AI agent with Wonder for subscribers and will develop specialized models it “can bring to everyone using Muse.” No further details or timelines were provided.

The announcement was reported by The Verge.
summary: Meta announced the release of two new AI models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, which are available to Muse Code subscribers starting today. The Wonder model can also be accessed via the Meta Model API, and Meta plans to eventually power its Muse AI agent with Wonder while developing specialized models for all Muse users.
author: The Verge

title: Amazon runs over 1 million robots as it scales operations
content:
Amazon has deployed more than one million robot workers, making it the second‑largest corporate employer to rely heavily on automation.  

The company has “bet big on robot workers to scale,” using the extensive fleet of machines to expand its operations.
summary: Amazon has over 1 million robot workers. The second-largest corporate employer has bet big on robot workers to scale.
author: Ars Technica

title: Google unveils Fitbit Edge, positioned between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air
content:
Google announced the Fitbit Edge, describing it as a device that sits between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air in its product lineup.  

According to the announcement, the Edge provides more functionality than the Air model, though the company notes it does not qualify as a full smartwatch.
summary: Google announced the Fitbit Edge as a middle ground between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air. The device offers more features than the Air but is not considered a real smartwatch.
author: Ars Technica

title: F1 Singapore sprint introduces new fastest car and first wet race of the year
content:
Singapore’s Formula 1 weekend produced a new benchmark for speed, with officials noting that a new fastest car has emerged on the circuit.  

The event’s final sprint also marked the season’s first genuine wet‑weather race, delivering the inaugural real wet racing of the year.
summary: The final sprint race in Singapore featured a new fastest car. It was the first real wet racing of the year in F1.
author: Ars Technica

title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
content: Russian bloggers have warned that Russia’s hyper‑centralized digital economy is vulnerable, indicating the country was unprepared for the data‑center conflict it launched with Ukraine. The commentary highlights concerns that the concentration of digital infrastructure could expose Russia to operational and security challenges amid the ongoing dispute.
summary: Russian bloggers warn Russia’s hyper-centralized digital economy is vulnerable.
author: Ars Technica

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 begins tomorrow with ticket savings up to $100
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 kicks off tomorrow at 8 a.m. PT, gathering more than 10,000 founders, investors and technology operators at San Francisco’s Moscone West.

The three‑day conference will feature ideas, connections and startups that aim to shape the next wave of technology.

Attendees have a final 24‑hour window to obtain ticket discounts of up to $100, with an additional offer of 50 % off a second ticket.
summary: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 kicks off tomorrow at 8 a.m. PT at San Francisco’s Moscone West, gathering 10,000+ founders, investors and tech operators for three days of ideas and connections. It is the final 24‑hour window to save up to $100 on tickets and get 50% off a second ticket.
author: TechCrunch

title: Google launches Fitbit Edge wearable priced at $179.99
content:
Google has launched the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable positioned as a middle ground between its Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch models.

The Fitbit Edge is priced at $179.99 and offers a sleek feel reminiscent of the Fitbit Air, while featuring an OLED display.
summary: Google’s newest wearable, the Fitbit Edge, is positioned between the Fitbit Air and the Pixel Watch. It costs $179.99 and features a sleek feel like the Fitbit Air with an OLED display.
author: TechCrunch

title: Honeyjar launches AI tools to improve PR and communications for companies
content:
Honeyjar has launched a suite of artificial‑intelligence tools designed to enhance public‑relations and communications functions across companies. The company positions its technology as a way to address criticisms that the PR process is broken, a view echoed by journalists, entrepreneurs and some public‑relations professionals.

The new AI solutions aim to streamline PR workflows and improve messaging, responding to industry calls for better, more efficient communications practices.
summary: Honeyjar is offering AI tools aimed at enhancing public relations and communications for companies. Journalists, entrepreneurs and some public relations professionals say the PR process is broken, raising the question of whether AI can make it better.
author: TechCrunch

title: WindBorne wins nearly $50 million US Air Force contract for balloon data
content:
WindBorne, a Silicon Valley startup that employs weather balloons and artificial‑intelligence technology to forecast weather, has been awarded a contract by the U.S. Air Force.  

The agreement is valued at almost $50 million, reflecting the military’s procurement of the company’s balloon‑derived data for weather prediction purposes.
summary: WindBorne, a Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather, won a U.S. Air Force contract. The contract is worth almost $50 million.
author: TechCrunch

title: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier AI model
content:
Meta has unveiled its first frontier model, named Muse Wonder. The new model follows the company’s earlier Muse Spark, which was designed as a lightweight, low‑latency solution.

According to Meta, the Wonder models are larger than Muse Spark and are described as more capable. They achieve higher benchmark scores and deliver improved performance on complex tasks, including coding.
summary: Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier model. The Wonder models are larger and more capable than Muse Spark, achieving higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks such as coding.
author: TechCrunch

title: Sandi Toksvig calls Wikipedia deeply biased and backs rival encyclopedia
content:
Sandi Toksvig, the comedian, says Wikipedia is “deeply biased” and is supporting a rival platform. She points to the fact that only 19 % of the online encyclopedia’s biography entries are about women.

Toksvig attributes the bias to the composition of Wikipedia’s editors, describing them as “mostly white, middle‑aged, European men.” The encyclopedia, which is 25 years old, has faced criticism over the gender imbalance in its content.
summary: Comedian Sandi Toksvig says Wikipedia is deeply biased, noting only 19% of its biographies are of women. She is supporting a rival online encyclopedia.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Six parents say they are more cautious, limiting kids' social media and AI use
content:
Six parents say they have become “significantly more cautious” about their children’s use of social media and artificial‑intelligence tools, opting to limit exposure as concerns grow.

Many parents no longer trust tech firms, noting that social‑media companies have spent much of the past decade asserting that their platforms are safe for teens, a claim that several families remain unconvinced about. Alongside a rising number of regulators, these parents have accused companies such as Meta of designing products that are addictive for younger users.
summary: Six parents say they have become significantly more cautious and are limiting their children’s use of social media and AI. They say they do not trust tech companies, noting that regulators and parents have accused firms such as Meta of creating products that are addictive to younger users.
author: Guardian Technology

title: UK AI minister warns AI-driven cyber attack like Australia OpenAI breach likely
content:
A senior UK minister warned that an AI‑driven cyber‑attack akin to the OpenAI breach of Australia’s healthcare system is “likely, if not inevitable” in Britain. Kanishka Narayan, the UK AI minister, said the British government’s own cyber defences could be bypassed by an artificial‑intelligence agent with highly sophisticated cybersecurity capabilities.

Narayan cited the Australian incident as a cause for concern and indicated that similar technology could compromise UK systems. She emphasized the risk that such AI‑based tools pose to national cyber security.
summary: UK AI minister Kanishka Narayan said an AI‑driven cyber‑attack similar to the OpenAI breach of Australia’s healthcare system is likely, if not inevitable, in the United Kingdom. He warned that the technology could bypass the British government’s own cyber defences.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Midday October 12, 2026 news bulletin highlights top European and global stories
content:
A news bulletin titled “Latest news bulletin | October 12th, 2026 – Midday” was issued on October 12, 2026. The bulletin invites readers to catch up with the most important stories from Europe and beyond.

It highlights coverage across a range of topics, including world events, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel.
summary: The bulletin provides the most important stories from Europe and beyond on October 12, 2026. It covers world, business, entertainment, politics, culture and travel news.
author: Euronews

title: Citroën unveils electric 2CV concept, aims for road debut in two years
content:
Citroën unveiled an all‑electric concept that draws on the design of its iconic 2CV, signaling a plan to reintroduce the classic model to the market within the next two years.  

The compact vehicle blends retro styling cues with modern electric technology and is projected to be priced at around €15,000.
summary: Citroën has unveiled an all‑electric concept inspired by its iconic 2CV. The compact vehicle combines retro styling with modern electric technology, targets a launch within the next two years and is expected to start at around €15,000.
author: Euronews

title: Fire devastates Paris's 400-year-old covered food market
content:
A video released on social media shows the aftermath of a major overnight fire that engulfed Paris’s oldest covered food market, a historic site dating back to 1615.  

The footage captures extensive damage to the 400‑year‑old market, underscoring the scale of the blaze that struck the landmark venue.
summary: A major overnight fire swept through Paris’s oldest covered food market. The market, which dates back to 1615, was shown in footage after the blaze.
author: Euronews

title: UAE urges stronger Gulf defence after deadly Riyadh airport attacks
content:
Deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airport have prompted regional leaders to call for a stronger joint Gulf defence. The United Arab Emirates urged its Gulf partners to enhance collective security measures, while allies expressed support for Saudi Arabia in the wake of the incident.

Qatar warned that the broader conflict stemming from the airport attacks was harming global energy supplies, highlighting the wider economic implications of the unrest.
summary: The UAE called for stronger Gulf defence after deadly attacks on Riyadh’s airport, with allies backing Saudi Arabia. Qatar warned that the wider conflict was damaging global energy supplies.
author: Euronews

title: German firms plan infrastructure and green energy projects in Baku
content:
German industrial giants gathered in Baku to outline new infrastructure and green‑energy initiatives, with Siemens Energy among the firms exploring collaboration opportunities. The companies are assessing ways to support Azerbaijan’s transition to greener energy sources.

Azerbaijan has set a target to handle 30 million tonnes of transit cargo by 2030, a goal that the German firms say could be integrated with their proposed infrastructure and energy projects.
summary: German industrial giants, including Siemens Energy, are exploring opportunities to support Azerbaijan's green energy transition. Azerbaijan aims to handle 30 million tonnes of transit cargo by 2030.
author: Euronews

title: Paris's oldest covered food market in Marais gutted by overnight fire
content:
Paris’s oldest covered food market in the Marais was gutted by a major fire overnight, according to local reports. The blaze swept through the historic market, leaving traders devastated.

Authorities have opened an investigation into the incident, and officials indicated that the market could remain closed for several months while repairs and safety checks are completed.
summary: A major overnight fire tore through Paris’s oldest covered food market in the Marais, leaving traders devastated. An investigation is under way and the market may stay shut for months.
author: Euronews

title: Turning Point Surges 64% After Charlie Kirk's Death Amid Legacy Battle
content:
Midterms 2026 bring renewed focus to Turning Point USA as the organization grapples with the legacy of its founder, Charlie Kirk, who died a year ago. In the twelve months following Kirk’s death, the number of American universities with Turning Point chapters rose by 64 percent, according to a report by France 24.

At the same time, the group and the broader MAGA movement are experiencing internal strain. Far‑right figures are competing for Kirk’s legacy, and conspiracy theories about his death are circulating among supporters. France 24 traveled to Phoenix, Arizona — the city where Turning Point was founded — to gauge how activists on the ground view the future of the conservative youth movement and who, if anyone, might assume Kirk’s mantle.
summary: In the year following the death of Charlie Kirk, the number of American universities with Turning Point chapters surged by 64 percent. France 24 travelled to Phoenix, Arizona, the birthplace of Turning Point, to investigate the division within the organization and the MAGA movement as far‑right figures vie for Kirk's legacy and conspiracy theories circulate about his death.
author: France 24

title: Paris Motor Show opens as Chinese car sales surge in Europe, intensifying competition
content:
The biennial Paris Motor Show opened this Monday in France, drawing more than 200 auto‑sector brands to compete for attention with their latest models and innovations.  

The showcase’s intense display of new vehicles mirrors the broader battle for market share between local European manufacturers and Chinese automakers. Chinese brands have experienced a surge in sales across the continent over the past decade, a trend that has sparked accusations of unfair competition.  

The report was written by Charles Pellegrin, France 24’s business editor.
summary: The biennial Paris Motor Show officially opened Monday in France, featuring more than 200 auto sector brands. The event underscores a rivalry between European manufacturers and Chinese car makers, whose sales have surged across the continent in the past ten years, prompting accusations of unfair competition, according to a report by Charles Pellegrin of FRANCE 24.
author: France 24

title: Saudi Arabia extends Riyadh airport closure amid Houthi drone and missile attacks
content:
Saudi Arabia announced on Monday that the closure of Riyadh’s international airport would remain in effect as the Saudi‑led coalition prepared a response to recent Houthi drone and missile attacks.

The latest Houthi assault on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300, prompting the coalition’s vow of a “deadly response.” Officials described the airport shutdown as one of the most severe disruptions to Saudi aviation in years and a marked escalation in the conflict with Yemen’s Houthi rebels.

The report and analysis were provided by France 24 international affairs editor Philip Turle.
summary: Saudi Arabia extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport on Monday after the Saudi‑led coalition said it was responding to combined Houthi drone and missile attacks. The latest Houthi strike on Saturday killed 13 people and injured more than 300, causing one of the worst disruptions to Saudi aviation in years.
author: France 24

title: Thousands march to Supreme Court in New Delhi demanding election chief resign
content:
Thousands of Indians marched to the Supreme Court in New Delhi, demanding the removal of the country’s top election commissioner. The protest continued as demonstrators took to the streets, calling for the commissioner’s resignation.

The unrest follows an investigation published in a leading newspaper that disclosed internal concerns about the revision of voter lists. The report, cited by protesters, has intensified frustrations within the election body.

The demonstration was reported by Delano D'Souza.
summary: Thousands of protesters in New Delhi marched to the Supreme Court demanding the country's top election commissioner resign. The unrest follows a newspaper investigation that said concerns were raised within the election body over revisions to voter lists.
author: France 24

title: Fire destroys historic Marché des Enfants‑Rouges market in Paris
content:
A fire that broke out overnight destroyed the iconic Marché des Enfants‑Rouges in Paris. The covered market, long adored by locals and tourists alike, is believed to be the oldest food market in the city.

The blaze caused no casualties, but the market’s vendors lost everything. The historic site’s irreplaceable heritage was also destroyed. The incident was reported by Charli James.
summary: The iconic Marché des Enfants‑Rouges in Paris was ravaged by fire overnight. No casualties were reported, but the market’s vendors lost everything and the historic market, believed to be the oldest food market in Paris, is irreplaceable.
author: France 24

title: Raphaël Glucksmann says battle begins to unite fragmented French left
content:
French presidential candidate Raphaël Glucksmann said on Monday that the “battle begins” to revive the country’s fragmented left ahead of the 2027 election.  

The EU lawmaker was elected on Sunday as the centre‑left candidate, securing more than 66 percent of the vote.
summary: Raphaël Glucksmann, a French presidential candidate, said Monday the battle begins to revive the country's divided left ahead of the 2027 election. He was elected Sunday as the centre‑left candidate with more than 66 percent of the vote.
author: France 24

title: Saudi Arabia faces increased drone and missile attacks from Yemen's Houthis
content:
Saudi Arabia’s vulnerability is being examined as Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthi movement intensifies its drone and missile campaign, targeting the kingdom’s critical infrastructure.  The analysis focuses on physical and material damage inflicted on Saudi airports and oil facilities and considers how such strikes could affect Riyadh’s capacity to project power.

The piece raises questions about the broader implications of cheap drone warfare for a nation that has long been seen as the region’s wealthiest and most secure state, probing how a battle‑hardened militia might challenge Saudi Arabia’s strategic standing.
summary: The piece evaluates Saudi Arabia’s exposure to the Houthis’ expanding drone and missile campaign. It discusses possible damage to airports and oil facilities and the impact on Riyadh’s ability to project strength.
author: France 24

title: Two high-ranking Iranian defectors give DW a rare look into the mindset of the regime's loyal servants
content:
DW’s investigative unit says it has spent months corresponding with two high‑ranking Iranian defectors. The extended dialogue, the outlet reports, has given the team a rare glimpse into the mindset of the regime’s loyal servants.

According to DW, the defectors disclosed details about a clandestine circle that they say is planning murders. The investigation highlights the alleged existence of this secret group within Iran’s power structure.
summary: Months of correspondence with two high-ranking defectors have given DW's investigative unit a rare look at the mindset of the regime's loyal servants — and revealed a clandestine circle that allegedly plots murders.
author: DW World

title: Cyprus deemed ready for Schengen but Green Line and UK bases pose hurdles
content:
The European Commission has stated that Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area.  

However, the island’s division along the Green Line and the presence of British Sovereign Base Areas remain political hurdles that could complicate its accession to Europe’s border‑free travel zone.  

These unresolved issues may affect the timeline for Cyprus’s entry into the Schengen system.
summary: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Questions about the Green Line division and the British Sovereign Base Areas could still complicate its path to the border‑free zone.
author: DW World

title: South Korea and Ukraine clash over secret transfer of two North Korean POWs
content:
Seoul and Kyiv are engaged in a diplomatic dispute after two North Korean prisoners of war were transferred to South Korea. Both governments have exchanged accusations over the handling of the transfer.

South Korea maintains that the move was intended to remain secret in order to avoid antagonising Pyongyang. The secrecy claim underscores the sensitivity of the issue for the South Korean authorities.
summary: Seoul and Kyiv are trading accusations after the transfer of two North Korean POWs to South Korea. South Korea says the move was kept secret to avoid antagonizing Pyongyang.
author: DW World

title: Starlink cleared approvals but remains in regulatory limbo in India
content:
Starlink, the satellite internet service owned by Elon Musk, has obtained key approvals in India but has not yet received the final regulatory clearance needed to launch. The service remains in a regulatory limbo despite those approvals.

The delay has prompted scrutiny over security clearances, the competitive landscape and the broader investment climate in India, all of which are now influencing the timing of Starlink’s entry into the market.
summary: Starlink has secured key approvals for its satellite internet service in India. However, the service stays in regulatory limbo amid questions about security clearances, competition and India’s investment climate.
author: DW World

title: DW Fact Check: Viral Riyadh airport attack videos are AI‑generated
content:
A fact‑check by DW has determined that widely shared videos purporting to show an attack on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport are not authentic.  

The clips, which circulated online claiming to depict the alleged assault, were examined by DW’s fact‑checking team. Their analysis of the most‑shared footage uncovered evidence that the videos were generated using artificial‑intelligence technology.  

DW concludes that the viral videos are fabricated and do not represent a real attack on the Riyadh airport.
summary: Many videos claiming to show an attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport have gone viral online. DW Fact Check found that the most‑shared footage was created using AI.
author: DW World

title: Poland says two Turkish citizens arrested in Germany over Starlink station fire
content:
Polish authorities announced that two Turkish citizens have been arrested in Germany in connection with the alleged sabotage of a Starlink station fire that occurred last month.

The arrests were reported as part of an investigation into the incident, which Polish officials say involved intentional damage to the satellite communications facility.

Prime Minister Donald Tusk described the fire as an act of “hybrid warfare.”
summary: Polish authorities reported that two Turkish citizens were arrested in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station fire last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."
author: DW World

title: UK Prime Minister says Iran likely behind RAF Fairford incident
content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament that there were “strong indications” of Iranian involvement in the incident at RAF Fairford, saying it was “highly likely” Iran was behind the event.

The UK government responded by summoning Iran’s ambassador to convey its concerns over the alleged involvement.

The scare at RAF Fairford prompted the withdrawal of United States Air Force B‑1 heavy bombers from the base.
summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were strong indications of Iranian involvement in the RAF Fairford incident. The government summoned Iran's ambassador and the scare led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.
author: DW World

title: UN rights office urges India to release arbitrarily detained protesters
content: The United Nations human rights office (OHCHR) has urged India to release individuals it says were “arbitrarily detained” in connection with recent protests. The office expressed concern over reports that demonstrators, protest leaders, civil‑society members, lawyers and journalists were detained in mass before and during large‑scale protests in Delhi on Saturday.
summary: The UN human rights office (OHCHR) voiced concern over reports of mass detentions in India. The detentions involved demonstrators, protest leaders, civil society members, lawyers and journalists before and during large‑scale protests in Delhi on Saturday.
author: UN News

title: Adam Ouattara and Makongo Traoré work toward peace with dam in Côte d’Ivoire
content:
Adam Ouattara and Makongo Traoré live with their four children in a home on the edge of Torla village in Côte d’Ivoire. He works as a cattle herder while she cultivates vegetables on a small plot nearby.

During the dry season, the couple’s two livelihoods have repeatedly come into conflict, as the scarcity of water and grazing land pits cattle herding against vegetable farming.
summary: Adam Ouattara and Makongo Traoré live on the edge of Torla village in Côte d’Ivoire and have four children. He herds cattle while she grows vegetables on a nearby plot, and the dry season has long pitted their livelihoods against each other.
author: UN News

title: UN chief Guterres condemns Houthi missile strike on Riyadh airport that killed 12
content:
UN Secretary‑General António Guterres condemned a missile strike launched by Yemen’s Houthi forces on Riyadh’s main airport, calling for an immediate end to the attacks.

Saudi authorities reported that the strike killed 12 people and injured more than 300 others.
summary: UN Secretary‑General António Guterres condemned a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh’s main airport. Saudi authorities say the strike killed 12 people and wounded more than 300.
author: UN News

title: Gaza residents Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin strive to sustain livelihoods amid war challenges
content:
Three residents of Gaza—Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin—are each pursuing personal initiatives despite the extraordinary challenges of living in a war‑ravaged enclave. Their stories, though different, are united by a common determination to build something of their own and keep it going.

The trio’s efforts illustrate how individuals in Gaza are striving to sustain livelihoods amid the ongoing crisis, reflecting a broader resolve to maintain economic activity despite the hardships imposed by the conflict.
summary: Nidaa, Hanaa and Hanin each have different stories. All three are determined to build something of their own and keep it going despite extraordinary challenges in war‑ravaged Gaza.
author: UN News

title: UN development chief warns rise in multidimensional poverty hits 1.2 billion
content:
The United Nations development chief warned that the recent increase in poverty is “a wake‑up call for the world,” after data showed a rise in the number of people living in “multidimensional” poverty.

For the first time in 15 years, the count of those in multidimensional poverty climbed to 1.2 billion, reflecting families’ growing difficulty in meeting basic needs.
summary: The UN development chief said the rise in poverty is a wake‑up call for the world. The number of people living in multidimensional poverty rose for the first time in 15 years to 1.2 billion as families struggle to meet basic needs.
author: UN News

title: UNHCR chief warns refugee protection buckling amid funding shortfall
content:
UNHCR chief warns that the global refugee protection system is under strain as funding falls short of growing needs.  

The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) currently faces a shortfall, having received only $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year to support 117 million men, women and children displaced from their homes.  

Barham Salih, the agency’s chief, cautions that the system for asylum‑seekers risks buckling under these cuts.
summary: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) has received only $3 billion of the $8.5 billion it needs this year. Chief Barham Salih warns that the global support system for asylum‑seekers risks buckling.
author: UN News

title: UN launches aid operation in Nepal after fresh Gorkha district floods
content:
The United Nations has launched an aid operation in Nepal after fresh flash floods struck the central Gorkha district on Sunday. The sudden flooding swept away homes and bridges in the area.

The disaster comes only weeks after catastrophic flooding in Nepal’s northern region. UN teams are now rushing to provide assistance to those affected by the latest floods.
summary: The United Nations has rushed to assist Nepal after new flash floods in the central Gorkha district on Sunday. The floods swept away homes and bridges, occurring just weeks after catastrophic flooding in the north.
author: UN News

title: Balkan temperatures swing dramatically as heavy rain heads for Greece
content:
Temperatures across the Balkans swung dramatically last week, with clear skies delivering warm daytime highs and cold overnight lows, especially in Montenegro. An area of high pressure over the region produced prolonged sunshine during the day, while the lack of cloud cover at night allowed heat to escape rapidly, creating an unusually large diurnal temperature range.

A low‑pressure system is now moving toward the Aegean Sea, a development linked to the forecast of heavy rain heading for Greece. The system’s approach follows the recent pattern of high‑pressure‑driven temperature swings in the Balkans.

The contrasting weather patterns—sunny, warm days and sharp cooling at night—highlight the region’s volatile climate conditions as the low‑pressure system advances.
summary: Temperatures in the Balkans fluctuated dramatically last week, with unusually large differences between daytime highs and overnight lows. Clear skies brought warm days and cold nights to Montenegro while a low‑pressure system moves toward the Aegean Sea, bringing heavy rain to Greece.
author: Guardian World

title: Fugitive businessman taken into US custody in Venezuela bribery case
content:
Alvaro Pulido, a businessman sought by U.S. authorities for allegedly bribing Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts, has been taken into custody.

Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021. The charges were part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, who was a one‑time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.

The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration and the State Department had offered a reward of up to $10 million for information that would lead to Pulido’s arrest.
summary: A businessman wanted in the US for allegedly bribing top Venezuelan officials has been taken into custodyA businessman wanted for years in the US for allegedly paying bribes to top Venezuelan officials in exchange for lucrative state contracts in Venezuela has been taken into custody. Alvaro Pulido was indicted in Miami federal court in 2019 and again in 2021 as part of an investigation into his longtime business partner, Alex Saab, a one-time ally of ousted Venezuelan president Nicolás Maduro.
author: Guardian World

title: Egypt's press union chief rejects pressure amid six Matsadaash journalists' torture claims
content:
Egypt’s press union chief has dismissed claims of pressure surrounding the detention of journalists, saying the union will not yield to external demands.

Six reporters affiliated with the independent platform Matsadaash have alleged that they were subjected to torture while in custody. Egyptian authorities have denied the accusations.
summary: Six journalists from the independent platform Matsadaash allege they were tortured while in detention. Egypt denies the allegations and its press union chief has rejected pressure over the detained journalists.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UK accuses Iran of airbase plot and sanctions two Iranian nationals
content:
The United Kingdom has blamed Iran for an alleged airbase plot and has imposed sanctions on two Iranian nationals.  

Iran’s ambassador to the UK informed officials that Tehran is willing to assist in the investigation and reiterated that Iran denies any involvement.
summary: The United Kingdom has blamed Iran for a plot targeting an airbase and sanctioned two Iranian nationals. Iran’s ambassador said Tehran is willing to assist the investigation and denied involvement.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cuba advances renewable energy plans despite US oil blockade
content:
Cuba is advancing its renewable energy agenda despite a U.S. oil blockade, according to recent statements.

The Cuban energy minister denied any connection to fuel shipments that were intercepted by the United States. He also said that oil imports by private firms are insufficient to meet the country’s needs.
summary: Cuba is pursuing renewable energy plans despite a U.S. oil blockade. The Cuban energy minister denied any link to the fuel shipments intercepted by the United States and said oil imports by private firms were insufficient.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pope Leo to have lung nodule surgery in Rome
content:
Pope Leo is scheduled to undergo surgery in Rome to remove a lung nodule. The 71‑year‑old Catholic leader will be treated at a hospital in the city.

The Vatican has announced that the Pope is expected to spend one week in the hospital for recovery before he begins his planned tour of Latin America.
summary: Pope Leo, the 71-year-old Catholic leader, will undergo surgery in Rome to remove a lung nodule. The Vatican expects his hospital recovery to last about one week before his scheduled Latin America tour.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Tom Cruise film Digger drops 60% in second weekend, forecast as major flop
content:
Tom Cruise’s film Digger is being forecast as one of Hollywood’s biggest flops after a steep decline in box‑office performance.  

The movie’s earnings fell by roughly 60 % in its second weekend, prompting analysts to predict it could rank among the industry’s most significant commercial failures.
summary: The film dropped by around 60% in its second weekend. It is forecast to become one of Hollywood's biggest flops.
author: BBC World

title: Immigration agents search Congresswoman Ilhan Omar's home
content:
Immigration agents conducted a search of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s home.  

Omar, identified in the report as an outspoken critic of former President Donald Trump, described the search as “an attempt to target political enemies.” She added that she “will not be silenced.”
summary: Immigration agents searched the home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar. Omar, an outspoken Trump critic, said the search was an attempt to target political enemies and that she will not be silenced.
author: BBC World

title: Robert Pattinson Stars as Real-Life Host of 'To Catch a Predator' in New Film
content: Actor Robert Pattinson stars in the new film Primetime, where he portrays the real-life host of the American television series To Catch a Predator. The movie explores the narrative of how the practice of hunting predators transformed into a popular television format.
summary: Robert Pattinson portrays the real-life host of the American TV show 'To Catch a Predator' in his new film Primetime. The film features his portrayal of the show's host.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Browns' Deshaun Watson Sacked Eight Times in Dismal Defeat, Hype Over Revival Punctured
content:
Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson suffered a significant setback in a recent loss to the New York Jets, ending a streak of three consecutive game-winning drives. The defeat dispelled recent narratives suggesting a revival for both Watson and the Browns, as the team struggled offensively against the Jets.

Watson’s performance was marked by a lack of production, completing fewer than 50% of his passes for just 155 passing yards and one touchdown. He finished the game with a 69.6 QBR and was sacked eight times, a figure that NBC NFL writer Patrick Daugherty described as an “unspeakably bad” performance. The quarterback completed only seven more passes than the number of times he was hit behind the line of scrimmage.
summary: Deshaun Watson, Cleveland's quarterback, completed less than 50% of his passes, threw one touchdown, and was sacked eight times in a 155‑yard performance that ended in a loss. The defeat dashed the hype surrounding Watson's revival and left the Browns unchanged.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Junior Nsemba aims to inspire young black people at Rugby League World Cup
content:
Junior Nsemba, a 22-year-old forward for Wigan, is described as one of England’s brightest hopes and a must-see talent for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup. The article highlights his strong desire to send a positive message and inspire young black people, stating that he wants to show that individuals can rise above hate.

England’s players will begin their World Cup campaign with an opening match this Saturday. Nsemba’s participation is expected to draw significant attention from fans and viewers, with the piece noting that the eyes of the world will be on him over the next month.
summary: Wigan forward Junior Nsemba is described as one of England's brightest hopes for the upcoming Rugby League World Cup. The 22-year-old states he wants to show that people can rise above hate and inspire young black individuals.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester City Triumphs Over Liverpool in 3-0 Victory Amid Controversy
content:
Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action

Manchester City secured a 3‑0 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, a result that has sparked both praise and controversy. The win was described as a vindication for City, while critics highlighted the club’s legal issues, including a charge of more than 100 offences that has been cited as damaging to the Premier League’s reputation.

Other weekend highlights included Crystal Palace’s 3‑1 win over Nottingham Forest and a 2‑2 draw between Hull City and Everton. The matches were reported by John Brewin. Enzo Maresca, speaking about the club’s situation, referred to the surrounding noise as “noise,” noting that the victory did not reduce the volume.
summary: Manchester City defeated Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield, a win that was both vindication and vilification. Enzo Maresca described the club’s plight as “noise” but said the victory did nothing to reduce it.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Sonay Kartal defeats Anhelina Kalinina in straight sets at Wuhan Open after injury return
content:
Britain’s Sonay Kartal has returned to form after her injury lay‑off, winning a straight‑sets victory over Anhelina Kalinina to advance to the second round of the Wuhan Open.  

The win, which saw Kartal take a top‑50 scalp, demonstrates her continued improvement since her return and secures her place in the next round of the tournament.
summary: Britain's Sonay Kartal defeated Anhelina Kalinina in straight sets at the Wuhan Open. The win brings her into the second round after returning from injury.
author: BBC Sport

title: More than 60 overs lost from South Africa vs Australia Test after ICC rule change
content:
More than 60 overs were lost from the first Test between South Africa and Australia, a loss that has drawn attention to the effectiveness of a recent change by the International Cricket Council (ICC).  

The overs were forfeited despite the ICC’s recent rule adjustment, suggesting the change may not have addressed the problem of bad light.  

The incident has prompted questions about whether cricket has missed a trick.
summary: More than 60 overs were lost from the first Test between South Africa and Australia after a rule change by the ICC. The article questions whether cricket has missed a trick.
author: BBC Sport

title: Senate Whip John Barrasso calls reports on Ambassador Guilfoyle very troubling
content:
Sen. John Barrasso (R‑Wyo.), the Senate Majority Whip, on Sunday expressed concern about recent reporting on U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle and her finances.  

Barrasso said the reports are “very troubling” and “concerning,” adding that he is sure there will be an investigation. He added, “I would assume the State Department would be…”
summary: Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso said the recent reports on U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle’s finances are very troubling. He said he expects an investigation, likely by the State Department.
author: The Hill

title: Trump’s Russian diesel import deal fuels struggle to prove cost‑of‑living focus
content:
President Trump is facing criticism for a new agreement to import millions of tons of diesel fuel from Russia. The deal has raised concerns among voters about the administration’s priorities.  

The move has made it difficult for the president to demonstrate that he is focused on the cost of living as the midterm elections approach.
summary: President Trump has a deal to import millions of tons of diesel fuel from Russia. He is struggling to show voters that he is focused on the cost of living ahead of the midterms.
author: NPR Politics

title: Rejecting closer EU ties would be dereliction of duty, PM to say
content:
The Prime Minister is set to address the House of Commons and warn that rejecting closer ties with the European Union would amount to a dereliction of duty.

In his speech, Burnham is expected to argue that a new deal with the EU could help tackle illegal immigration and boost economic growth.
summary: Addressing the Commons, Burnham is expected to say that a new deal with the EU could help tackle illegal immigration and boost economic growth.
author: BBC Politics

title: IPCC meeting to set next report date as some countries delay emissions cuts
content:
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) is convening to determine the schedule for its next major report. The meeting comes amid efforts by some countries to postpone the release and dilute the urgency for accelerated emissions reductions.  

The article, titled “Governments that support climate science must stand firm against naysayers,” was published on Climate Home News.
summary: The IPCC is meeting to decide the timing of its next major report. Some countries are trying to delay the report and weaken the case for faster emissions cuts.
author: Climate Home News

title: Younger breast cancer patients under 40 face higher odds of delayed diagnosis
content:
A recent analysis of data on adolescents and young adults with breast cancer found that lower income and younger age were linked with delays in care. The study, published online in the journal Cancer, examined patients diagnosed before age 40 and identified socioeconomic and age-related factors that contributed to postponed treatment.

The research also showed that women who experienced delays in cancer diagnoses tended to have later‑stage disease at the time of treatment. This suggests that delayed care may lead to more advanced cancer when it is finally identified.

The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to reduce diagnostic delays among younger, lower‑income breast cancer patients.
summary: In an analysis of data on adolescents and young adults with breast cancer, lower income and younger age were linked with delays in care. Women who experienced delays in cancer diagnoses tended to have later-stage disease.
author: Medical Xpress

title: VUB study finds hot days nearly doubled in Congo Basin over past two decades
content:
New research led by scholars at Vrije Universiteit Brussel (VUB) and published in the journal Earth System Dynamics finds that hot days have become almost twice as common in the Congo Basin over a twenty‑year span.  

The study identifies a clear warming signal across the basin dating back to the 1960s, based on rescued historical weather records. These records were sourced from the paper archives of the Institut National pour l'Etude et la Recherche Agronomiques (INERA) in Yangambi, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and from the State Archives of Belgium.  

The analysis of the rescued data indicates a marked increase in the frequency of hot days, highlighting accelerating climate change impacts in the region.
summary: New research led by Vrije Universiteit Brussel and published in Earth System Dynamics shows a clear warming signal across the Congo Basin since the 1960s. Analysis of rescued historical weather records from the Institut National pour l'Etude et la Recherche Agronomiques in Yangambi and the State Archives of Belgium indicates that hot days have become nearly twice as common in the basin over the past two decades.
author: Phys.org

title: Italian rice farmer Alice Cerutti restores a third of fields for biodiversity
content:
Italian rice farmer Alice Cerutti is converting a portion of her fields in northwest Italy back to natural marshland. Four hundred years after monks first turned the area’s marshes into rice paddies, Cerutti has restored about one‑third of the cultivated land to its original state.

The restoration emphasizes biodiversity rather than maximizing crop yield, marking a shift toward ecological stewardship in the historic rice‑growing region.
summary: Four hundred years after monks transformed a patch of marshlands in northwest Italy into rice fields, farmer Alice Cerutti has restored a third of the fields to their natural state. She is prioritizing biodiversity over crop yield.
author: Phys.org

title: El Niño breaks temperature record in key Pacific zone, EU monitor says
content:
El Niño broke a temperature record in a key Pacific zone in September, the European Union’s climate monitor said on Monday.  

The monitor noted that the intensifying El Niño is gaining “exceptional strength,” as evidenced by the new temperature high.
summary: An intensifying El Niño broke a temperature record in a key Pacific zone in September. The EU's climate monitor reported the record on Monday, noting the weather pattern’s growing strength.
author: Phys.org

title: World leaders urged to course correct as UN biodiversity goals fall short
content:
World leaders have been urged to “course correct” after UN nature goals were found to be falling short, according to a report ahead of the upcoming U.N. Biodiversity summit. The warning comes as nations prepare for what many expect to be a disappointing report card on their environmental commitments.

Governments are reported to be missing their pledges to protect plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth, prompting calls for stronger action at the summit this month.
summary: Nations are preparing for a disappointing report card at this month’s UN Biodiversity summit. Governments are falling short on their commitments to protect plants, animals and ecosystems.
author: Phys.org

title: Hurricane Simon shifts course, expected to skirt Mexico's west coast
content:
Hurricane Simon altered its trajectory slightly on Sunday, moving farther offshore along Mexico’s western shoreline. Meteorologists forecast that the storm will skirt the coast without making landfall.

Despite staying at sea, Simon is expected to bring heavy rain and severe winds to the region as it continues its offshore path.
summary: Hurricane Simon shifted track slightly on Sunday. It was forecast to skirt Mexico's west coast without making landfall while packing heavy rain and severe winds.
author: Phys.org

title: Strongest El Niño since 1870s sparked global famine, prompting preparedness questions
content:
The world is currently facing an El Niño event that experts say is the strongest since the 1870s, a period when the climate pattern triggered a severe global famine.  

The unprecedented intensity of the present El Niño has raised questions about whether modern societies are better equipped to handle its impacts compared with the historic crisis of the 19th century.
summary: The world has not experienced an El Niño this strong since the 1870s, when it triggered a severe global famine. The piece questions whether humanity is better prepared for such an event today.
author: New Scientist

title: UT Austin researchers find 10 minutes daily exercise boosts deep sleep
content:
Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin reported that modest daily exercise may improve deep, restorative sleep. The study found that individuals who exercised more frequently experienced greater amounts of deep sleep, which the researchers noted is essential for brain recovery, memory and emotional well‑being.

According to the findings, just 10 minutes of moderate‑to‑vigorous activity each day was associated with measurable sleep benefits. Even lighter activities such as walking and taking standing breaks were linked to better sleep and mood.

The results suggest that brief, regular physical activity could help enhance sleep quality.
summary: Researchers at The University of Texas at Austin found that people who exercised more frequently got more deep, restorative sleep, which supports brain recovery, memory and emotional well‑being. The study showed that just 10 minutes of moderate‑to‑vigorous activity a day, or even light activities such as walking and standing breaks, were linked to better sleep and mood.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find universe's constants finely balanced to support life
content:
Scientists have reported that the universe’s fundamental physical constants appear to be finely balanced in a way that makes life possible. The research suggests that even minute alterations to these constants could change the viscosity of liquids, rendering them too thick or too thin for essential biological processes and potentially precluding life as we know it.  

The study indicates that such life‑friendly conditions existed billions of years before the emergence of living cells, implying that the physical environment suitable for life was present long before biology arose.  

These observations raise questions about why the laws of physics seem so well suited to supporting life.
summary: Scientists discovered that the universe's fundamental physical constants may be finely balanced to make life possible. They said tiny changes could alter liquid properties needed for biology and that these life‑friendly conditions existed billions of years before living cells appeared.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists link declining Menin protein to aging and show D-serine boosts mouse memory
content:
Scientists reported that a decline in the protein Menin may be a hidden driver of aging. In experiments with older mice, restoring Menin levels reversed several age‑related changes within 30 days.

The researchers also found that supplementing the mice’s diet with the amino acid D‑serine improved memory and learning performance. The results suggest D‑serine could represent a new approach to combat age‑related cognitive decline.
summary: Scientists discovered that declining levels of the protein Menin may help drive aging and that restoring Menin in older mice reversed several age‑related changes within 30 days. They also found that supplementing older mice with the amino acid D‑serine improved memory and learning, suggesting a possible approach to age‑related cognitive decline.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists find vanillin may fight infections, reduce inflammation and aid wound healing
content:
Scientists have discovered that vanillin, the compound responsible for vanilla’s distinctive flavor, possesses powerful biological properties. The research indicates that vanillin can help fight infections, reduce inflammation and promote wound healing.

The inexpensive, widely available ingredient could one day become an important component of advanced wound treatments and regenerative medicine.
summary: Scientists discovered that vanillin, the compound giving vanilla its flavor, has powerful properties that could help fight infections, reduce inflammation, and promote wound healing. The inexpensive, widely available ingredient could one day become an important component of advanced wound treatments and regenerative medicine.
author: Science Daily

title: GLP-1 weight loss drugs Ozempic and Wegovy linked to increased nail loss
content:
Popular GLP-1 weight‑loss medications, including Ozempic and Wegovy, have been associated with a notable increase in nail detachment, hair loss and scalp inflammation, according to recent research. The study found that these adverse effects occurred several times more often among users of the drugs than in the general population.

Researchers determined that the degree of weight loss alone could not fully account for the elevated rates of these symptoms, indicating that additional factors related to the medications may be involved. The findings highlight a set of overlooked side effects that may affect patients using GLP‑1 therapies.
summary: Popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy have been linked to unusually high rates of nail detachment, hair loss, and scalp inflammation. Researchers said weight loss alone could not fully explain the differences, suggesting other factors may contribute.
author: Science Daily

title: Roman fort discovered in Pembrokeshire may confirm Magnus Maximus camp near Frenni Fawr
content:
Archaeologists have identified a previously unknown Roman fort in Pembrokeshire, Wales, near Frenni Fawr hill, where medieval folklore has long spoken of a camp founded by the fourth‑century emperor Magnus Maximus.  

Excavations at the site have uncovered fourth‑century Roman coins and other artefacts, providing material evidence that supports the legend of a military encampment linked to Maximus, who is known to have led troops against the Picts and Scots.  

The discovery suggests the medieval tale of a camp on Frenni Fawr hill may be rooted in historical reality, exciting researchers studying Roman activity in Britain.
summary: Archaeologists have identified a Roman fort in Pembrokeshire that yielded fourth‑century coins. The discovery supports the medieval folklore that Emperor Magnus Maximus established a camp near Frenni Fawr hill.
author: Guardian Science

title: Wooden circular table serves as setting for today’s puzzle
content:
A new puzzle described as “a puzzle for the ages” centers on an object that is made of wood, shaped like a circle, and traditionally serves as the forum for many important gatherings.  

The wooden, circular setting is identified as the backdrop for today’s riddle, inviting readers to solve the challenge presented.
summary: The puzzle describes an object that is made of wood, shaped like a circle, and serves as a forum for many important gatherings. That object is the setting for today’s puzzle.
author: Guardian Science

title: Mars passes near Beehive (M44) cluster, serving as signpost this week
content:
Mars will appear very close to the Beehive cluster, or Praesepe, from a dark location this week. The red planet acts as a signpost for observers looking for the faint, misty patch of stars.

The Beehive, catalogued as Messier 44, lies in the constellation Cancer. It has been known since antiquity, when its hazy appearance earned it the Latin name Praesepe, meaning a manger or crib. Although it is one of the brightest star clusters in the night sky, it can be surprisingly difficult to locate because Cancer contains no bright stars to guide the eye toward it.

This week, Mars provides a convenient reference point for locating the cluster.

title: Show HN: BraiNOTES lets users annotate lecture PDFs directly in a browser tab
content:
Show HN: BraiNOTES is a browser‑only tool that lets users write handwritten notes directly on lecture PDFs without leaving the tab. The static website runs completely offline, storing every change in IndexedDB and never sending data to a server or analytics service. It supports free‑hand strokes with pen‑pressure sensitivity and renders PDFs with pdf.js in a worker thread.

BraiNOTES offers two main modes. In Study mode the PDF appears beside the note area, allowing users to read and snip formulas or diagrams into the notes with a snip tool before writing around them. Board mode provides a whiteboard for tutoring or extra exercise space, with a laser‑pointer tool for presentations. Ink appears instantly as the pen moves, and a lightweight filter smooths shaky strokes while a light refit corrects the line when the pen is lifted. Notebooks can be exported as Brainotes files—a zip containing a JSON per page, the original PDFs, and any imported images—while keeping the underlying text selectable.

The project is hosted on GitHub under the MIT license (https://github.com/swimmingbrain/brainotes) and can be tried at https://notes.swimmingbrain.dev. The author, who has used the tool for every lecture in recent months and has a few friends adopting it, also works on a video editor, animation tool, and an MCP server that can be enabled locally for further automation. Bug reports, fixes, and feedback are welcome; the discussion can be followed on Hacker News (https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50049132).
summary: BraiNOTES is a static, offline‑first website that lets users open lecture PDFs in a browser tab and write handwritten notes on them with a pen, without requiring an account or backend. It stores strokes in IndexedDB after each change, supports pen pressure and a one‑euro filter for smooth ink, offers Study and Board modes, and can export notebooks as a zip containing JSON pages, the original PDFs, and any imported images.

title: Kimi Antonelli says he can taste F1 glory after Singapore GP podium
content:
Kimi Antonelli said he can finally dare to dream of a Formula One world championship after finishing third at the Singapore Grand Prix. Max Verstappen led the race at Marina Bay from start to finish and won with a dominant drive.

Antonelli’s podium puts him in a position to become F1’s youngest champion at the age of 20 if he wins the next round in Austin. He leads Mercedes teammate George Russell by 102 points and Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton by 111 points.

title: Maresca hails City after 3-0 Anfield win
content:

Enzo Maresca praised the side for “making their own noise” and said, “You cannot imagine how happy I am … I’m here to win.” The win came as City brushed aside the controversy and threats surrounding the club.

The result kept City’s unbeaten start to the season intact, with goals from Erling Haaland, Jérémy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It marked a sixth successive league win for the team and preserved their position at the top of the Premier League table.

With the victory, Maresca equalled the best start to a managerial reign in Premier League history, maintaining the club’s 100 % record in the league to date.

content:

content:

content: A pilot study presented at the European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) annual congress in Munich found that low doses of LSD may improve sustained attention in women but not in men. The researchers reported that the effects were gender‑specific, with women showing potential gains in sustained attention while men showed no such improvement. The findings are preliminary and were shared at the congress, adding to growing evidence that individuals may respond differently to psychedelic microdosing.
summary: A pilot study indicates low doses of LSD may improve sustained attention in women but not in men. The results were presented at the ECNP annual congress in Munich and are preliminary.

title: Very severe long COVID linked to distinct mouth and lung microbiome differences
content:

The research shows that these distinct bacterial communities in the lung microbiome are associated with the respiratory symptoms that patients experience. It also links the microbiome differences to the cognitive and digestive problems that are commonly reported in long COVID.
summary: A study of more than 700 people found that patients with very severe long COVID have distinct differences in the bacteria that live in their mouths and lungs. These differences in the lung microbiome are associated with respiratory symptoms as well as the cognitive and digestive problems known to occur in long COVID.

title: Elgin Community College requests Flock to remove cameras; Flock refuses
content:

In October 2025, Elgin’s president, Peggy Heinrich, formally requested that Flock remove its cameras.

summary: Elgin Community College asked Flock to remove six safety cameras installed in 2025 because the school was concerned that Flock was sharing data with Customs and Border Patrol, that camera feeds were not properly secured, and that both law enforcement and the company's employees were abusing access to the data. summary: Manchester City defeated Liverpool 3-0 at Anfield in their first match after being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The victory extended City's perfect start to six matches, moving them three points clear at the top of the league.

title: Zelensky Awaiting U.S. Details on Trump-Announced Energy Ceasefire
content:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated on Sunday that Kyiv is awaiting specific details from Washington regarding an energy ceasefire with Russia. This response introduces uncertainty over the agreement, which U.S. President Trump had previously claimed had already taken effect.

Zelensky emphasized that Ukraine supports the ceasefire and noted that it is important for Russia to support it as well. The Ukrainian leader’s comments highlight the current status of negotiations, with Kyiv waiting for further information from the United States to proceed.
summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Kyiv is waiting for details from Washington about an energy ceasefire with Russia that President Trump announced. Zelensky stated Ukraine supports the ceasefire and wants Russia to support it as well.

title: Officials urge U.S. AI policy to protect American data from China
content:
Former officials Juan Caro and Peter Brown contend that U.S. artificial intelligence policy needs to be reformed to safeguard sensitive personal data from foreign adversaries, specifically China. They argue that current approaches risk allowing American data to empower foreign nations rather than protecting domestic interests.

According to the officials, a balanced strategy is required to foster technological innovation while ensuring that Americans' personal information remains secure. They emphasize that AI should ultimately empower Americans, not provide a competitive advantage to China through data access.
summary: Former officials Juan Caro and Peter Brown argue that U.S. AI policy must protect Americans' sensitive personal data from foreign adversaries like China. They assert that this protection is necessary while fostering technological innovation.

title: Massie backs Trump’s diesel deal with Russia
content:
Rep. Thomas Massie (R‑Ky.) publicly endorsed President Trump’s diesel deal with Russia on Sunday, a rare stance given the two politicians’ prior disagreements.  

Massie, who voted against Russia sanctions in 2022, cited concerns that U.S. citizens would face higher prices. He said he was glad to see Trump “came around to that reality this week” and added that sanctions should be lifted.  

The statement was made on Sunday.
summary: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) backed President Trump’s diesel deal with Russia on Sunday, despite their past conflict. He had voted against Russia sanctions in 2022, pointing out that U. S. Citizens would suffer from higher prices, and now calls for lifting sanctions.

title: Russia Hits Kharkiv Power Plant After Trump Announces Energy Ceasefire
content:
President Trump announced on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire,” but Russia subsequently struck a power plant in eastern Ukraine, contradicting the claim. A local official told ABC News that a thermal power plant in Kharkiv was hit twice and is currently on fire.

Ukrainian President Voldoymyr Zelensky confirmed the attack on the facility.

content:
